  <!-- composer as before -->
</section>

@if (pendingApproval(); as approval) {
  <app-approval-dialog [pending]="approval" (decided)="onApprovalDecided($event)" />
}
  readonly pendingApproval = this.chat.pendingApproval;

  readonly lastCitations = computed(() => {
    const assistant = this.messages().filter((m) => m.role === 'assistant');
    return assistant.at(-1)?.citations ?? [];
  });

  readonly lastChunks = computed(() => this.chat.lastChunks());

  onApprovalDecided(approved: boolean): void {
    this.chat.respondToApproval(approved);
  }

  onOpenSource(citation: Citation): void {
    this.router.navigate(['/documents'], {
      queryParams: { source: citation.source, chunk: citation.chunk_id },
    });
  }
Line(s)What it doesWhy we need it
@if (pendingApproval(); as approval)Binds the non-null value to a local name.The as form narrows the type inside the block, so [pending]="approval" satisfies a required non-null input. Without it the compiler correctly objects.
trace viewer placed after each bubblePer-message trace, not one global panel.Each answer has its own steps. A single panel would show only the latest and lose the history you would want when comparing two answers.
assistant.at(-1)?.citations ?? []Citations from the most recent answer..at(-1) is cleaner than [length - 1] and returns undefined rather than throwing on an empty array.
respondToApproval(approved)Sends the decision back to the server.The part that needs backend support. The agent is blocked mid-loop, so this needs a second endpoint — a POST that resolves the pending decision, keyed by a run id. Part 10 wires it; conceptually it is section 6.4's approve callback, split across the network.
router.navigate with query paramsJumps to the documents page at the cited chunk.Makes the citation genuinely checkable rather than decorative. Requires injecting Router.

M18 is done. git commit -m "M18: citations panel, trace viewer, approval dialog". Compare this against section 7.9's table: streaming, cancellation, markdown, sanitisation, citations, trace, approval — every one of the things the prototype tools hide, now written by you and under your control.

Try this yourself. Feed the citations panel a citation whose quote does not appear in the chunk. The red "not found in the retrieved text" warning appears. Now consider the design question that raises: should the answer even be shown? Section 5.7's server-side code filtered unverified citations out entirely, so this branch should be unreachable — which makes it a canary. If it ever fires in production, your two verification layers disagree and something is wrong. That is worth logging, not just displaying.

9.11 File upload with progress

Upload documents to the ingestion endpoint with a real progress bar and per-file state.

ng generate service core/documents
ng generate component features/documents/documents
import { HttpClient, HttpEventType } from '@angular/common/http';
import { Injectable, inject, signal } from '@angular/core';

import { environment } from '../../environments/environment';

export type UploadState = 'queued' | 'uploading' | 'indexing' | 'done' | 'failed';

export interface Upload {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  size: number;
  progress: number;          // 0-100
  state: UploadState;
  chunks?: number;
  error?: string;
}

@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class DocumentsService {
  private readonly http = inject(HttpClient);
  private readonly base = environment.apiBase;

  readonly uploads = signal<Upload[]>([]);

  private patch(id: string, changes: Partial<Upload>): void {
    this.uploads.update((list) =>
      list.map((u) => (u.id === id ? { ...u, ...changes } : u)),
    );
  }

  upload(file: File): void {
    const id = crypto.randomUUID();
    this.uploads.update((list) => [
      ...list,
      { id, name: file.name, size: file.size, progress: 0, state: 'queued' },
    ]);

    const form = new FormData();
    form.append('file', file, file.name);

    this.http
      .post<{ chunks: number }>(`${this.base}/api/documents`, form, {
        reportProgress: true,
        observe: 'events',
      })
      .subscribe({
        next: (event) => {
          if (event.type === HttpEventType.UploadProgress) {
            const total = event.total ?? file.size;
            this.patch(id, {
              state: 'uploading',
              progress: Math.round((100 * event.loaded) / total),
            });
          } else if (event.type === HttpEventType.Sent) {
            this.patch(id, { state: 'uploading' });
          } else if (event.type === HttpEventType.Response) {
            this.patch(id, {
              state: 'done',
              progress: 100,
              chunks: event.body?.chunks,
            });
          }
        },
        error: (err) => {
          this.patch(id, {
            state: 'failed',
            error: err.status === 413
              ? 'File too large for the API limit.'
              : err.error?.detail ?? `Upload failed (${err.status}).`,
          });
        },
      });
  }

  uploadAll(files: FileList | null): void {
    if (!files) return;
    Array.from(files).forEach((file) => this.upload(file));
  }
}
<section class="page">
  <h1>Documents</h1>

  <label class="drop"
         [class.over]="dragging()"
         (dragover)="onDragOver($event)"
         (dragleave)="dragging.set(false)"
         (drop)="onDrop($event)">
    <input type="file" multiple hidden
           accept=".pdf,.md,.txt"
           (change)="onPick($event)" />
    <span>Drop PDFs, markdown or text files here, or click to choose</span>
  </label>

  @for (item of uploads(); track item.id) {
    <article class="upload" [class.failed]="item.state === 'failed'">
      <div class="row">
        <span class="name">{{ item.name }}</span>
        <span class="size">{{ (item.size / 1024) | number: '1.0-0' }} KB</span>
        <span class="state">{{ item.state }}</span>
      </div>

      @if (item.state === 'uploading' || item.state === 'indexing') {
        <progress [value]="item.progress" max="100"
                  [attr.aria-label]="'Uploading ' + item.name"></progress>
      }

      @if (item.state === 'done') {
        <p class="ok">Indexed as {{ item.chunks }} chunks.</p>
      }
      @if (item.error) {
        <p class="err">{{ item.error }}</p>
      }
    </article>
  } @empty {
    <p class="empty">No uploads yet.</p>
  }
</section>
import { DecimalPipe } from '@angular/common';
import { Component, inject, signal } from '@angular/core';

import { DocumentsService } from '../../core/documents.service';

@Component({
  selector: 'app-documents',
  imports: [DecimalPipe],
  templateUrl: './documents.html',
  styleUrl: './documents.scss',
})
export class Documents {
  private readonly docs = inject(DocumentsService);

  readonly uploads = this.docs.uploads;
  readonly dragging = signal(false);

  onPick(event: Event): void {
    this.docs.uploadAll((event.target as HTMLInputElement).files);
  }

  onDragOver(event: DragEvent): void {
    event.preventDefault();
    this.dragging.set(true);
  }

  onDrop(event: DragEvent): void {
    event.preventDefault();
    this.dragging.set(false);
    this.docs.uploadAll(event.dataTransfer?.files ?? null);
  }
}

  border-radius: 12px;
  color: #5b6472;
  cursor: pointer;
  transition: border-color 0.15s, background 0.15s;

  &.over { border-color: #2f4bd8; background: #f2f5ff; }
  &:focus-within { outline: 2px solid #2f4bd8; outline-offset: 2px; }
}

.upload {
  margin-top: 1rem;
  padding: 0.75rem;
  border: 1px solid #dcdfe4;
  border-radius: 8px;

  &.failed { border-color: #c0392b; }
}

.row { display: flex; gap: 0.75rem; align-items: baseline; font-size: 0.9rem; }
.name { flex: 1; font-weight: 600; overflow-wrap: anywhere; }
.size, .state { color: #5b6472; font-size: 0.8rem; }

progress { width: 100%; height: 0.5rem; margin-top: 0.5rem; }

.ok  { color: #1d7a4c; font-size: 0.85rem; margin: 0.4rem 0 0; }
.err { color: #c0392b; font-size: 0.85rem; margin: 0.4rem 0 0; }
.empty { color: #5b6472; margin-top: 1.5rem; }
Line(s)What it doesWhy we need it
reportProgress: true, observe: 'events'Makes HttpClient emit progress events instead of just the final response.Both options are required. With only reportProgress you still get one response and no progress. This is the whole mechanism.
event.type === HttpEventType.UploadProgressDiscriminates the event kind.The observable now emits several event types, so you must narrow. TypeScript will not let you read event.loaded until you do.
event.total ?? file.sizeFalls back when the total is unknown.total is optional in the type. Dividing by undefined gives NaN, and a progress bar showing NaN is a memorable bug.
new FormData() with no Content-Type headerMultipart upload.Do not set Content-Type yourself. The browser must add it with the multipart boundary; setting it manually omits the boundary and the server cannot parse the body. A classic hour-long debugging session.
'indexing' as a distinct stateUpload finished, server still working.Honest UX: after the bytes arrive, your backend still has to chunk and embed (section 5.6), which can take longer than the upload. A bar stuck at 100% looks broken. ⚠ Reporting real indexing progress needs a server-side job status endpoint or an SSE stream — the same transport as 9.7.
err.status === 413Special-cases "payload too large".The error you will actually hit with PDFs. Both nginx and FastAPI impose limits; Part 10 raises them.
<label> wrapping a hidden <input type="file">A styled drop zone that is still a real file input.Clicking the label opens the picker, keyboard focus works, and screen readers announce it. Much better than a div with a click handler that opens a hidden input.
accept=".pdf,.md,.txt"Filters the picker.A hint, not a guarantee — drag-and-drop bypasses it and it is client-side. The server must validate too.
event.preventDefault() in both drag handlersStops the browser's default behaviour.Without it on dragover, the drop never fires; without it on drop, the browser navigates away to open your PDF. Both are required.
| number: '1.0-0' with DecimalPipeFormats the size with no decimals.Pipes must be imported into standalone components — hence imports: [DecimalPipe]. Forgetting that is a common early error.
<progress>, not a styled divThe native element.Accessible by default and announced as a progress bar. [attr.aria-label] names which file, since several may upload at once.
uploadAll looping over filesOne request per file, concurrently.Simple and it gives per-file progress and per-file failure. For dozens of files you would want a concurrency limit — otherwise you open 40 simultaneous connections.
overflow-wrap: anywhere on the nameWraps long filenames.A 90-character filename would otherwise stretch the card and break the layout.
Try this yourself. Upload a large PDF and watch the bar reach 100% and sit there while your backend chunks and embeds it. That gap is the 'indexing' state doing its job. Now consider that section 5.6's ingestion took 2.4 seconds for 84 chunks — for a 300-page PDF it is minutes, which is an argument for a background job and a status stream rather than a blocking request.

9.12 Environments, proxy, and the CORS fix

Environment files

ng generate environments
export const environment = {
  production: false,
  // Empty string means "same origin", so the dev-server proxy handles it.
  apiBase: '',
};
export const environment = {
  production: true,
  // In production, nginx serves the app and proxies /api to the API container.
  apiBase: '',
};

The dev-server proxy — the fix that avoids CORS entirely

{
  "/api": {
    "target": "http://localhost:8000",
    "secure": false,
    "changeOrigin": true,
    "logLevel": "debug"
  }
}
"serve": {
  "options": {
    "proxyConfig": "proxy.conf.json"
  }
}
Line(s)What it doesWhy we need it
apiBase: ''Requests go to /api/... on the same origin.The key idea. The browser sees a same-origin request to localhost:4200, so CORS never applies. The dev server forwards it to port 8000 server-side, where CORS is not a concept.
"/api" as the proxy keyAny path starting /api is forwarded.Which is why every backend route in Part 10 is namespaced under /api. One rule covers all of them.
"changeOrigin": trueRewrites the Host header to the target.Needed when the target checks the host. Harmless otherwise, so leave it on.
"secure": falseAccepts self-signed TLS certificates.Only relevant if your API is HTTPS in development.
"logLevel": "debug"Prints proxied requests in the ng serve terminal.Invaluable: it tells you immediately whether a 404 came from Angular or from FastAPI.
Same apiBase in both environmentsProduction also uses a relative path.nginx serves the static files and proxies /api to the API container (Part 10, M19). Identical code path in both, which removes a whole class of "works in dev" bug.

⚠ Verify the proxy option location. Where proxyConfig lives in angular.json has moved between builder versions, and recent CLIs may scaffold it differently. If the proxy is not picking up, run ng serve --proxy-config proxy.conf.json explicitly — if that works, the file is fine and the angular.json placement is wrong.

CORS, for when you cannot use a proxy

If you point apiBase directly at http://localhost:8000, the browser applies the same-origin policy: different port means different origin, so the request needs the server's permission. What actually goes wrong, in order:

SymptomCauseFix
Console: "blocked by CORS policy: No 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header", and err.status === 0The server sent no CORS headers.Add the FastAPI middleware below.
A GET works but the POST failsThe POST triggers a preflight: the browser sends OPTIONS first because of the Content-Type: application/json header.The middleware must allow the OPTIONS method and the Content-Type header. Check devtools' Network tab for a failing OPTIONS request — people miss it because it is not the request they wrote.
Everything works until you add an auth headerCustom headers must be explicitly allowed.Add it to allow_headers.
Cookies are not sentCredentialed requests need allow_credentials on the server and withCredentials on the client.And note: with credentials enabled, the wildcard origin * is forbidden by the spec. You must list origins explicitly.
Streaming works with curl but not the browserNot CORS. Something is buffering.Set X-Accel-Buffering: no on the SSE response and check any proxy in between.
 
from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware

app = FastAPI()

# Development only. In production the frontend is same-origin behind nginx,
# so this middleware should not be needed at all.
app.add_middleware(
    CORSMiddleware,
    allow_origins=["http://localhost:4200"],   # never ["*"] with credentials
    allow_credentials=True,
    allow_methods=["GET", "POST", "OPTIONS"],
    allow_headers=["Content-Type", "Authorization"],
)
Line(s)What it doesWhy we need it
allow_origins=["http://localhost:4200"]An explicit origin list.Must match exactly — scheme, host and port. http://localhost:4200 and http://127.0.0.1:4200 are different origins, which is a genuinely confusing half hour the first time.
allow_credentials=TruePermits cookies and auth headers.Forces you off the wildcard origin, per the specification. Set it to False if you do not need cookies, and you may then use ["*"] in development.
allow_methods=[..., "OPTIONS"]Allows the preflight.The preflight is an OPTIONS request. Omit it and every POST fails while GETs work — the most confusing CORS symptom there is.
allow_headers=["Content-Type", ...]Allows the headers we actually send.Content-Type: application/json is what makes a POST "non-simple" and triggers the preflight in the first place.
the comment about productionSays this is a development crutch.Worth being explicit: if your production frontend is served from the same origin as the API, CORS never applies and this middleware is dead configuration. Leaving a permissive CORS policy in production is a real, common security mistake.

Which to use. Use the proxy in development — it sidesteps CORS entirely, it matches how production works, and it means one fewer thing configured in two places. Keep the CORS middleware for the case where the frontend really is on a different origin, and configure it narrowly when you do.

Thing to noticeWhy it matters
"Estimated transfer size" is roughly a third of rawThat is gzip. Judge budgets on transfer size, not raw.
chat and documents are lazy chunksThe loadComponent routes from 9.5 working. Someone landing on /documents never downloads the markdown libraries.
marked and dompurify are in the chat chunkBecause only the chat feature imports them. Import them in the root component instead and they move into main, hurting first load for no reason.

Budgets, which fail the build rather than nagging

"budgets": [
  { "type": "initial", "maximumWarning": "300kB", "maximumError": "600kB" },
  { "type": "anyComponentStyle", "maximumWarning": "6kB", "maximumError": "12kB" }
]

The CLI scaffolds these. Raising them because the build failed is the wrong instinct — the failure is the feature. Find out what grew: ng build --stats-json then feed dist/.../stats.json to a bundle analyser such as esbuild-visualizer. ⚠ The stats format depends on the builder, so check what your version emits.

The four things that actually keep an AI frontend small

  1. Lazy-load every route. Already done in 9.5, and it is the biggest single win.
  2. Lazy-load highlight.js. Section 9.8's deeper dive. Import it inside an await import() after streaming completes, and only the language cores you need.
  3. Do not add a component library for four components. A full UI kit for a modal, a progress bar and a panel is a poor trade — and the native <details>, <progress> and <dialog> elements are accessible already.
  4. Check what a markdown library pulls in. marked is small; some alternatives bring a plugin ecosystem and a much larger footprint.

What ng build produces. A folder of static files — index.html, hashed JS and CSS, assets. No Node needed to serve it. That is what makes the multi-stage Docker build in Part 10 straightforward: build with Node, then copy the output into an nginx image and throw the Node layer away.

9.14 Testing, with the AI mocked out

⚠ A deliberate deviation from your brief. You asked for Jasmine and Karma. Karma is deprecated and no longer accepts fixes, and Angular 21+ ships Vitest as the default runner for new projects. Teaching a deprecated runner would be doing you a disservice, so the code below is Vitest — and the important news is that almost nothing changes:

  • describe, it, expect, beforeEach — identical.
  • TestBed, ComponentFixture, fixture.detectChanges() — identical.
  • Spies differ: jasmine.createSpyObj becomes vi.fn(), and spyOn(...).and.returnValue(x) becomes vi.spyOn(...).mockReturnValue(x).
  • If you are on an older project, the CLI has a migration schematic; check the current name for your version.

The concepts and the TestBed patterns transfer completely, so if your workplace is on Jasmine you will be productive immediately.

Test the message bubble and the chat service without a model, a network, or a GPU.

import { ComponentFixture, TestBed } from '@angular/core/testing';
import { describe, expect, it, beforeEach } from 'vitest';

import { ChatMessage } from '../../core/models';
import { MessageBubble } from './message-bubble';

function make(overrides: Partial<ChatMessage> = {}): ChatMessage {
  return {
    id: 'm1', role: 'assistant', text: 'Port 11434.',
    streaming: false, citations: [], steps: [],
    ...overrides,
  };
}

describe('MessageBubble', () => {
  let fixture: ComponentFixture<MessageBubble>;

  beforeEach(async () => {
    await TestBed.configureTestingModule({
      imports: [MessageBubble],
    }).compileComponents();

    fixture = TestBed.createComponent(MessageBubble);
  });

  function render(message: ChatMessage): string {
    fixture.componentRef.setInput('message', message);
    fixture.detectChanges();
    return (fixture.nativeElement as HTMLElement).textContent ?? '';
  }

  it('renders the answer text', () => {
    expect(render(make())).toContain('Port 11434.');
  });

  it('labels user and assistant differently', () => {
    expect(render(make({ role: 'user', text: 'hi' }))).toContain('You');
    expect(render(make())).toContain('Second Brain');
  });

  it('shows a thinking indicator before the first token', () => {
    const html = render(make({ text: '', streaming: true }));
    expect(html).toContain('Thinking');
  });

  it('shows the citation count once finished', () => {
    const html = render(make({
      citations: [{ source: 'setup.md', chunk_id: 4, quote: 'port 11434' }],
    }));
    expect(html).toContain('1 source');
  });

  it('shows an error and a retry button when the turn failed', () => {
    const html = render(make({ error: 'Cannot reach the API.' }));
    expect(html).toContain('Cannot reach the API.');
    expect(fixture.nativeElement.querySelector('button.retry')).toBeTruthy();
  });

  it('emits the message id when retry is clicked', () => {
    const emitted: string[] = [];
    fixture.componentRef.setInput('message', make({ id: 'abc', error: 'boom' }));
    fixture.componentInstance.retry.subscribe((id: string) => emitted.push(id));
    fixture.detectChanges();

    fixture.nativeElement.querySelector('button.retry').click();
    expect(emitted).toEqual(['abc']);
  });

  it('escapes HTML in user text rather than rendering it', () => {
    const html = render(make({ role: 'user', text: '<img src=x onerror=alert(1)>' }));
    expect(fixture.nativeElement.querySelector('img')).toBeNull();
    expect(html).toContain('<img');
  });
});
Line(s)What it doesWhy we need it
make(overrides) factoryBuilds a valid ChatMessage with one field changed.Each test says only what it cares about. Without this every test carries seven irrelevant fields, and adding a field to the interface breaks all of them.
TestBed.configureTestingModule({ imports: [MessageBubble] })Sets up a miniature Angular app around the component.Standalone components go in imports, not declarations. Older tutorials use declarations; that is the NgModule era.
fixture.componentRef.setInput('message', ...)Sets a signal input from a test.The API to know. Assigning fixture.componentInstance.message = x does not work — signal inputs are read-only from outside. This trips up everyone converting older tests.
fixture.detectChanges()Runs change detection and updates the DOM.Required after every input change. Forgetting it means asserting against the previous render, which produces baffling failures.
textContent assertionsTests what the user sees.Deliberately not testing computed values directly. A test that asserts isUser() is true passes even when the template forgot to use it.
retry.subscribe(...)Outputs are subscribable in tests.The way to assert a component emitted the right thing. Note we assert the id, which is the contract 9.3 chose.
the HTML-escaping testAsserts no <img> element exists and the literal text is shown.The most valuable test in the file. It encodes section 9.8's security decision as a regression test. If someone later "improves" user messages to render markdown, this test fails and explains why that is not an improvement.

Testing the service with a mocked HTTP layer

import { HttpTestingController, provideHttpClientTesting } from '@angular/common/http/testing';
import { provideHttpClient } from '@angular/common/http';
import { TestBed } from '@angular/core/testing';
import { describe, expect, it, beforeEach, afterEach } from 'vitest';

import { ChatService } from './chat.service';

describe('ChatService', () => {
  let service: ChatService;
  let http: HttpTestingController;

  beforeEach(() => {
    TestBed.configureTestingModule({
      providers: [provideHttpClient(), provideHttpClientTesting()],
    });
    service = TestBed.inject(ChatService);
    http = TestBed.inject(HttpTestingController);
  });

  afterEach(() => http.verify());

  it('adds a user message and a streaming placeholder', () => {
    service.ask('What port?');

    expect(service.messages().length).toBe(2);
    expect(service.messages()[0].role).toBe('user');
    expect(service.messages()[1].streaming).toBe(true);

    http.expectOne((r) => r.url.endsWith('/api/ask')).flush({
      answer: { answer: 'Port 11434.', confidence: 0.95, citations: [] },
      chunks: [],
    });

    expect(service.messages()[1].text).toBe('Port 11434.');
    expect(service.messages()[1].streaming).toBe(false);
    expect(service.busy()).toBe(false);
  });

  it('reports a helpful error when the API is unreachable', () => {
    service.ask('anything');

    http.expectOne((r) => r.url.endsWith('/api/ask'))
      .error(new ProgressEvent('error'), { status: 0, statusText: '' });

    expect(service.messages()[1].error).toContain('Cannot reach the API');
    expect(service.busy()).toBe(false);
  });

  it('never mutates the messages array in place', () => {
    const before = service.messages();
    service.addUserMessage('hello');
    expect(service.messages()).not.toBe(before);
  });
});
Line(s)What it doesWhy we need it
provideHttpClientTesting()Replaces the real HTTP backend with a controllable fake.No network, no model, no GPU, no flakiness. Note it must come after provideHttpClient() — it overrides the backend that call installed.
http.expectOne(...)Asserts exactly one matching request was made, and returns it.Also catches the opposite bug: if the service accidentally fires two requests, this fails.
.flush({...})Supplies the response body synchronously.Tests stay synchronous and instant. The body is shaped like the real AskResponse, so a backend contract change shows up here.
.error(new ProgressEvent('error'), { status: 0 })Simulates a network failure.Tests the branch you cannot easily reach otherwise, and pins the exact message from describe(). Status 0 is the CORS/unreachable case from 9.12.
afterEach(() => http.verify())Fails the test if any request went unanswered.Catches a service that fires a request nobody expected — a real bug that otherwise passes silently.
the "never mutates" testAsserts the array reference changed.Encodes the signals rule from 9.4 as a test. If someone later writes list.push(m), this fails with a clear reason rather than producing a mysteriously frozen UI.

What to test, and what not to

Test thisDo not bother
Rendering per state: streaming, done, failed, empty.That Angular renders a @for loop.
The HTML-escaping and sanitisation decisions.Exact CSS classes or pixel values.
The SSE parser against chunk boundaries — extract it into a pure function and feed it the byte-by-byte case from 9.7.Real network streaming in a unit test. Test the parser, not the transport.
Error message mapping for status 0, 429 and 5xx.That HttpClient works.
That the TypeScript models still match the API — a contract test against a recorded FastAPI response, or generated types from its OpenAPI schema.Handwritten assertions that duplicate the interface.
Try this yourself. Extract parseSseEvent and the buffering loop from 9.7 into a standalone exported function, then write a test that feeds it the sample stream one character at a time and asserts it produced exactly five events. That is the highest-value test in the whole frontend, because it is the one piece of logic that works locally and fails in production.

9.15 Part 9 checkpoint

Quiz answer 1: your UI does not update when the message text changes. Two likely causes?

(1) You mutated the array or object instead of replacing it — signals compare by reference, so list.push(m) or m.text += t changes nothing observable. (2) The value is a plain class field rather than a signal, and on a zoneless app (v21+ default) nothing tells Angular to look again. The rule from 9.3: if a template shows it, it is a signal, and you always produce a new reference.

Quiz answer 2: why fetch + ReadableStream rather than EventSource for chat?

EventSource is GET-only and cannot send custom headers. A chat question wants a POST body — conversation history will not fit in a URL — and you will eventually want an Authorization header. You give up automatic reconnection and have to parse the SSE framing yourself, which is the sixty lines in 9.7. Use EventSource for a server-push feed you did not initiate.

Quiz answer 3: your streaming parser works locally and drops tokens in production. Why?

You are splitting each network chunk independently instead of buffering across chunks. On localhost whole SSE events usually arrive in one read, so it appears to work; over a real network a read can contain half an event. The verified output in 9.7 shows the naive version producing four corrupted fragments instead of five events, the first being the truncated string event: token\ndata: {. Buffer, then split on the blank line.

Quiz answer 4: when is bypassSecurityTrustHtml acceptable?

Only when you have already sanitised the string yourself with a dedicated sanitiser such as DOMPurify — and even then, prefer plain [innerHTML] and let Angular sanitise as well. The reason this matters more in an AI app than a normal one: model output can quote a document you did not write, so <img src=x onerror=...> from a poisoned PDF becomes script execution in your own UI with your user's session. Our MarkdownService deliberately never calls it, so it cannot be copied carelessly.

Quiz answer 5: a GET works but every POST fails with a CORS error. What is happening?

The POST sends Content-Type: application/json, which makes it a "non-simple" request, so the browser first sends an OPTIONS preflight. Your server does not allow OPTIONS or does not allow that header, so the preflight fails and the real request is never sent. Look for the failing OPTIONS in the Network tab — people miss it because it is not the request they wrote. Better still, use the dev-server proxy from 9.12 and avoid CORS entirely.

Quiz answer 6: what should the approval dialog show, and why does it matter?

The tool name and every argument in full — for a file write, the entire content. A dialog saying "the agent wants to write a file. OK?" trains users to click yes, which is worse than having no gate, because now everyone believes there is one. Deny gets the focus, Escape denies, and the label says "Allow once" so no blanket permission is implied.

You are done with Part 9 when you can

  • Read a React AI tutorial and write the Angular equivalent without looking up the mapping.
  • Explain why signals need a new reference, and what zoneless changed.
  • Write the SSE buffering loop from memory and say what breaks without the buffer.
  • Make a Stop button that stops generation on the server, not just in the browser.
  • Explain the markdown-then-sanitise order and why the reverse is unsafe.
  • List the seven UI states of a chat turn.
  • Test a component and a service with no model, no network and no GPU.

PackageLicenceWhy

The SSE formatter — verified against the client

"""Format Server-Sent Events. The exact contract the Angular client parses."""

import json
from typing import Any


def sse(event: str, data: Any) -> str:
    """One SSE frame: named event, JSON payload, blank-line terminator."""
    payload = json.dumps(data, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"))
    lines = [f"event: {event}"]
    for line in payload.split("\n"):
        lines.append(f"data: {line}")
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n\n"


def sse_comment(text: str = "keep-alive") -> str:
    """A comment frame. Keeps proxies from closing an idle connection."""
    return f": {text}\n\n"


if __name__ == "__main__":
    frames = [
        sse("token", {"text": "Retrieval "}),
        sse_comment(),
        sse("token", {"text": "augmented "}),
        sse("token", {"text": "generation"}),
        sse("citations", [{"source": "setup.md", "chunk_id": 4, "quote": "port 11434"}]),
        sse("step", {"n": 1, "thought": "search", "tool": "search_notes",
                     "args": {"query": "port"}, "observation": "[...]", "ok": True}),
        sse("done", {"tokens": 63, "seconds": 4.9}),
    ]
    wire = "".join(frames)
    print(wire, end="")
    print(f"--- {len(frames)} frames, {len(wire)} bytes ---")
Line(s)What it doesWhy we need it
separators=(",", ":")Compact JSON with no spaces.Every byte is re-sent per token. Not a micro-optimisation at 60 events a second — it is a few percent of your bandwidth for free.
ensure_ascii=FalseEmits real UTF-8.Escaped sequences would inflate every non-English answer. The client decodes UTF-8 with TextDecoderStream (section 9.7), so this is safe.
for line in payload.split("\n")Splits a multi-line payload across several data: lines.Required by the SSE spec. A raw newline inside a data: line would be read as an event boundary and corrupt the stream. Compact JSON has no newlines, so this loop almost never fires — and it prevents a catastrophic bug when something eventually does.
+ "\n\n"The blank-line terminator.This is what the client's indexOf('\n\n') looks for. One newline instead of two and the browser buffers your entire answer.
sse_comment()Emits : keep-alive.Proxies and load balancers close idle connections, typically after 30–60 seconds. A local model can easily be silent that long while processing a long prompt. The client skips lines starting with :.

Verified: the Python formatter against the Angular parser

This is a genuine contract test — output from the Python above, fed to the JavaScript parser from section 9.7, delivered at three different chunk sizes.

Python formatter -> Angular parser contract test:
one chunk                events=6
chopped every 17 bytes   events=6
one byte at a time       events=6
identical across boundaries: true

parsed events:
  token      "Retrieval "
  token      "augmented "
  token      "generation"
  citations  1 item(s)
  step       n,thought,tool,args,observation,ok
  done       tokens,seconds

reassembled answer: "Retrieval augmented generation"

Six events (the keep-alive comment is correctly ignored), identical regardless of how the bytes are chopped up, and the tokens reassemble into the original answer. That is the two halves of your streaming stack agreeing.

The application

"""M15: the API the Angular client talks to."""

import asyncio
import logging
import time
import uuid
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager

from fastapi import FastAPI, File, HTTPException, Request, UploadFile
from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware
from fastapi.responses import StreamingResponse
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

from app.config import get_settings
from app.obs import LlmCallRecord, log_event, setup_logging, trace_id_var
from app.rag import answer_question, retrieve
from app.sse import sse, sse_comment

log = logging.getLogger("secondbrain.api")

SSE_HEADERS = {
    "Cache-Control": "no-cache",
    "Connection": "keep-alive",
    "X-Accel-Buffering": "no",
}


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):
    """Load the expensive things once, at startup."""
    setup_logging(get_settings().log_level)
    log_event(log, "startup", model=get_settings().chat_model)
    from app.embeddings import SentenceTransformerEmbedder
    app.state.embedder = SentenceTransformerEmbedder()
    yield
    log_event(log, "shutdown")


app = FastAPI(title="Second Brain", version="1.0.0", lifespan=lifespan)

settings = get_settings()
if not settings.production:
    app.add_middleware(
        CORSMiddleware,
        allow_origins=["http://localhost:4200"],
        allow_credentials=True,
        allow_methods=["GET", "POST", "OPTIONS"],
        allow_headers=["Content-Type", "Authorization"],
    )


@app.middleware("http")
async def add_trace_id(request: Request, call_next):
    """One id per request, on every log line and returned to the client."""
    trace_id = request.headers.get("x-trace-id") or str(uuid.uuid4())[:8]
    trace_id_var.set(trace_id)
    started = time.perf_counter()
    response = await call_next(request)
    response.headers["x-trace-id"] = trace_id
    log_event(
        log, "request.done",
        method=request.method, path=request.url.path,
        status=response.status_code,
        ms=round((time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000),
    )
    return response


class AskRequest(BaseModel):
    question: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=2000)
    top_k: int = Field(4, ge=1, le=10)


@app.get("/api/health")
async def health() -> dict:
    return {"ok": True, "model": settings.chat_model}


@app.post("/api/ask")
async def ask(body: AskRequest) -> dict:
    """Non-streaming answer. What section 9.5's M16 chat calls."""
    started = time.perf_counter()
    answer, chunks, problems = await asyncio.to_thread(
        answer_question, body.question, body.top_k,
    )
    log_event(
        log, "ask.done",
        seconds=round(time.perf_counter() - started, 2),
        citations=len(answer.citations),
        citation_problems=len(problems),
    )
    return {"answer": answer.model_dump(), "chunks": chunks}


@app.post("/api/chat/stream")
async def chat_stream(body: AskRequest, request: Request) -> StreamingResponse:
    """M17's endpoint: tokens as they are produced, stopping if the client leaves."""

    async def events():
        started = time.perf_counter()
        tokens = 0
        try:
            chunks = await asyncio.to_thread(retrieve, body.question, body.top_k)
            yield sse("citations", [
                {"source": c["source"], "chunk_id": c["chunk_id"], "quote": ""}
                for c in chunks
            ])

            from app.stream_async import astream_chat
            messages = build_messages(body.question, chunks)

            last_ping = time.perf_counter()
            async for fragment in astream_chat(messages):
                if await request.is_disconnected():
                    log_event(log, "stream.client_gone", tokens=tokens)
                    break

                tokens += 1
                yield sse("token", {"text": fragment})

                if time.perf_counter() - last_ping > 15:
                    last_ping = time.perf_counter()
                    yield sse_comment()

            yield sse("done", {
                "tokens": tokens,
                "seconds": round(time.perf_counter() - started, 2),
            })
        except asyncio.CancelledError:
            log_event(log, "stream.cancelled", tokens=tokens)
            raise
        except Exception as exc:                       # noqa: BLE001
            log.exception("stream.failed")
            yield sse("error", {"message": f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"})

    return StreamingResponse(events(), media_type="text/event-stream",
                             headers=SSE_HEADERS)


def build_messages(question: str, chunks: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:
    """Assemble the prompt from section 5.7's template."""
    from app.rag import SYSTEM, render_context
    return [
        {"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM},
        {"role": "user", "content": f"{render_context(chunks)}\n\nQuestion: {question}"},
    ]


@app.post("/api/documents")
async def upload_document(file: UploadFile = File(...)) -> dict:
    """Section 9.11's upload target."""
    if not file.filename:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="No filename supplied.")
    if not file.filename.lower().endswith((".pdf", ".md", ".txt")):
        raise HTTPException(status_code=415, detail="Only PDF, markdown and text.")

    payload = await file.read()
    if len(payload) > 25 * 1024 * 1024:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=413, detail="File larger than 25 MB.")

    chunks = await asyncio.to_thread(ingest_bytes, file.filename, payload)
    log_event(log, "document.ingested", name=file.filename,
              bytes=len(payload), chunks=chunks)
    return {"chunks": chunks}


def ingest_bytes(filename: str, payload: bytes) -> int:
    """Write to the docs folder and re-index. Returns the chunk count."""
    from pathlib import Path
    from app.build_index import main as rebuild

    target = Path("data/docs") / Path(filename).name
    target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    target.write_bytes(payload)
    return rebuild([])
Line(s)What it doesWhy we need it
lifespan as an async context managerRuns setup before serving and teardown after.Where the embedding model loads. Section 5.7's retrieve() constructed it per call — fine in a script, catastrophic per request. Everything before yield happens once. (This replaces the deprecated @app.on_event("startup").)
app.state.embedder = ...Stashes the loaded model on the app.The conventional place for expensive singletons in FastAPI. @lru_cache works too; app.state makes the lifetime explicit.
if not settings.productionCORS middleware only in development.Section 9.12's point: in production nginx makes everything same-origin, so a permissive CORS policy would be dead configuration and a real risk. Add production: bool = False to Settings.
@app.middleware("http") setting trace_id_varOne id per request, in a ContextVar.Every log line in that request carries it automatically — no threading it through every function. Returning it in a header means a user can quote it in a bug report.
request.headers.get("x-trace-id") or ...Honours an incoming id.Lets a trace span client and server, and later multiple services.
class AskRequest(BaseModel) with max_length=2000Validated request body.Your Part 1 Pydantic skills, now doing input validation at the edge. FastAPI returns a 422 with field-level detail automatically. The length cap is a first line of defence against someone pasting a novel into your context window.
await asyncio.to_thread(answer_question, ...)Runs blocking code on a worker thread.Critical. answer_question uses requests and sentence-transformers, both blocking. Calling it directly in an async def route freezes the entire event loop — section 1.4's failure at production scale, and the single most common FastAPI mistake.
the events() async generatorYields SSE frames.Exactly the AsyncIterator[str] shape from section 4.5. That function was written to be reused here unchanged.
yield sse("citations", ...) firstSends sources before any token.The citations panel populates while the answer is still being written, which makes the UI feel instant. Note the empty quote — the verified quotes arrive at the end, from the parsed structured answer.
if await request.is_disconnected(): breakDetects the browser hanging up.The other half of section 9.7's Stop button. Without this, aborting the fetch stops the display and the GPU keeps working. Breaking out closes the generator, which closes the httpx stream, which makes Ollama stop — section 4.5's with block, paying off.
the 15-second keep-aliveEmits a comment when nothing has been sent recently.Prevents an idle-timeout kill during a long prefill. 15 seconds is comfortably under the usual 30–60 second proxy default.
except asyncio.CancelledError: ... raiseLogs the cancellation and re-raises.Must re-raise. Swallowing CancelledError breaks async cancellation semantics and leaves tasks in a strange state. Log, then let it propagate.
yield sse("error", ...) in the handlerReports failures inside the stream.The HTTP status was already 200 when the first byte went out, so you cannot return a 500. Mid-stream errors must be events — which is why StreamEvent in section 9.2 has an error case.
media_type="text/event-stream"The SSE content type.Required. Without it browsers and proxies treat the response as a normal body and buffer it.
"X-Accel-Buffering": "no"Tells nginx not to buffer.The header that fixes "streaming works in curl but not in the browser". nginx buffers proxied responses by default, so your beautifully streamed tokens arrive in one lump. Costs nothing when nginx is absent.
"Cache-Control": "no-cache"Stops intermediaries caching the stream.A cached SSE stream is a memorable class of bug.
UploadFile = File(...)Declares a multipart file field.Matches the FormData field name file from section 9.11. FastAPI streams it to a spooled temporary file rather than holding it all in memory.
the extension and size checksValidates server-side.Section 9.11 noted the client accept attribute is only a hint. 413 and 415 are the statuses the frontend already handles.
rebuild([]) inside to_threadRe-indexes after an upload.Honest but crude: it rebuilds the whole index. Fine for a personal tool, wrong beyond that — see the warning below.

Run it

PYTHONPATH=backend uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8000

# then, in another terminal, prove streaming works before blaming the frontend:
curl -N -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/chat/stream \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"question":"What port does the Ollama API use?"}'
{"ts": "2026-09-01T09:14:02", "level": "INFO", "logger": "secondbrain.api", "trace_id": "-", "msg": "startup", "model": "qwen3:1.7b"}
INFO:     Uvicorn running on http://127.0.0.1:8000

# curl output, arriving progressively:
event: citations
data: [{"source":"setup.md","chunk_id":4,"quote":""}]

event: token
data: {"text":"The"}

event: token
data: {"text":" Ollama"}
...
event: done
data: {"tokens":24,"seconds":3.11}

curl -N is your first diagnostic, always. The -N disables curl's own buffering. If curl streams and the browser does not, the problem is nginx, the dev-server proxy, or a missing header — not your code. If curl does not stream either, it is the generator or a blocking call in the loop.

Two honest limitations of this endpoint. (1) Re-indexing on upload is synchronous and total. Section 5.6 took 2.4 seconds for 84 chunks; a 300-page PDF is minutes, and the HTTP request is held open the whole time. The real design is a background job plus a status stream — which is why section 9.11 has an 'indexing' state waiting for it. (2) There is no conversation history. Each request is standalone. Adding it means passing a session id and loading section 6.7's ConversationMemory — the pieces exist, the wiring is yours.

Common errors and how to fix them
ErrorCauseFix
The whole answer arrives at onceMissing X-Accel-Buffering, wrong media type, or a blocking call inside the loop.Test with curl -N first to find which side is buffering.
The server freezes under two concurrent usersBlocking code in an async def route.Wrap every blocking call in asyncio.to_thread. Or declare the route def rather than async def and FastAPI runs it in a threadpool for you.
RuntimeError: Form data requires "python-multipart"Missing dependency.uv pip install python-multipart.
Stop in the browser but the GPU keeps workingNo is_disconnected() check.Add it inside the token loop. Verify by watching ollama ps after cancelling.
Client hangs forever with no done eventAn exception escaped the generator before the final yield.The except that yields an error event covers it. Always terminate the stream with something.
422 on every request from AngularBody field names do not match the Pydantic model.Read the 422 body — FastAPI names the offending field. Or check /docs, which FastAPI generates for you.
Try this yourself. Open http://localhost:8000/docs. FastAPI has generated an interactive OpenAPI page from your Pydantic models. Now fetch http://localhost:8000/openapi.json — that document can generate your TypeScript interfaces automatically, which closes the "the two type definitions drifted" gap that section 9.2 warned about. Tools like openapi-typescript do it in one command.

10.3 The approval round-trip

Section 6.4's agent loop called approve(tool, args) and blocked. Across a network that becomes: the stream emits an approval event, the agent waits, the browser shows the dialog from 9.10, and a second HTTP request delivers the answer.

"""Pause an agent mid-run until a human answers. Single-process only."""

import asyncio
from dataclasses import dataclass, field


@dataclass
class PendingDecision:
    tool: str
    args: dict
    event: asyncio.Event = field(default_factory=asyncio.Event)
    approved: bool = False


class ApprovalRegistry:
    """Keyed by run id. One in-flight decision per run."""

    def __init__(self, timeout_seconds: float = 300.0) -> None:
        self.timeout = timeout_seconds
        self._pending: dict[str, PendingDecision] = {}

    def create(self, run_id: str, tool: str, args: dict) -> PendingDecision:
        decision = PendingDecision(tool=tool, args=args)
        self._pending[run_id] = decision
        return decision

    async def wait(self, run_id: str) -> bool:
        """Block until decided, or deny on timeout. Fail closed."""
        decision = self._pending.get(run_id)
        if decision is None:
            return False
        try:
            await asyncio.wait_for(decision.event.wait(), timeout=self.timeout)
            return decision.approved
        except asyncio.TimeoutError:
            return False
        finally:
            self._pending.pop(run_id, None)

    def resolve(self, run_id: str, approved: bool) -> bool:
        """Called by the HTTP endpoint. Returns False if nothing was waiting."""
        decision = self._pending.get(run_id)
        if decision is None:
            return False
        decision.approved = approved
        decision.event.set()
        return True


registry = ApprovalRegistry()
from app.approvals import registry


class ApprovalDecision(BaseModel):
    run_id: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=64)
    approved: bool


@app.post("/api/approvals")
async def decide(body: ApprovalDecision) -> dict:
    """Section 9.10's respondToApproval() target."""
    delivered = registry.resolve(body.run_id, body.approved)
    if not delivered:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=409, detail="No decision is pending for that run.")
    log_event(log, "approval.decided", run_id=body.run_id, approved=body.approved)
    return {"ok": True}


@app.post("/api/agent/stream")
async def agent_stream(body: AskRequest, request: Request) -> StreamingResponse:
    """The full agent loop, streamed, with a human gate on risky tools."""
    run_id = str(uuid.uuid4())[:12]

    async def approve(tool: str, args: dict) -> bool:
        registry.create(run_id, tool, args)
        return await registry.wait(run_id)

    async def events():
        yield sse("run", {"run_id": run_id})
        queue: asyncio.Queue = asyncio.Queue()

        async def emit(event: str, data: dict) -> None:
            await queue.put((event, data))

        task = asyncio.create_task(
            run_agent_async(body.question, approve=approve, emit=emit, run_id=run_id)
        )

        while True:
            try:
                event, data = await asyncio.wait_for(queue.get(), timeout=15.0)
            except asyncio.TimeoutError:
                if await request.is_disconnected():
                    task.cancel()
                    break
                yield sse_comment()
                continue

            yield sse(event, data)
            if event in {"done", "error"}:
                break

        if not task.done():
            task.cancel()

    return StreamingResponse(events(), media_type="text/event-stream",
                             headers=SSE_HEADERS)
Line(s)What it doesWhy we need it
asyncio.Event per decisionA one-shot flag a coroutine can await.The agent's approve() awaits it; the HTTP endpoint sets it. This is the whole mechanism, and it is why the agent can block without blocking the server.
asyncio.wait_for(..., timeout=self.timeout)Gives up after five minutes.Without a timeout, a user who closes the tab leaves a coroutine waiting forever, holding memory and an open connection.
except asyncio.TimeoutError: return FalseTimeout means deny.Fail closed, exactly as section 6.4's approve=None default did. Silence is never consent.
finally: self._pending.pop(...)Always cleans up.Otherwise abandoned runs accumulate and a stale run_id could be resolved later.
resolve() returning a booleanReports whether anything was waiting.Lets the endpoint return 409 rather than silently accepting a decision nobody asked for — which would otherwise hide a frontend bug.
yield sse("run", {"run_id": run_id})Sends the run id first.The client must know it to post a decision. First event, before anything can need approval.
asyncio.Queue plus create_taskThe agent runs as a task and pushes events into a queue the generator drains.The structural point. The agent loop is a normal function that calls emit(); it knows nothing about HTTP. The generator turns queue items into SSE frames. Section 6.4's loop stays reusable.
wait_for(queue.get(), timeout=15.0)Waits for the next event, or times out to send a keep-alive.An agent can spend a minute in one tool call. Without this the connection looks idle and a proxy kills it.
if await request.is_disconnected(): task.cancel()Cancels the agent when the client leaves.An abandoned agent loop keeps calling models and tools. This is the difference between a cancel that saves money and one that only hides the output.
if not task.done(): task.cancel()Belt and braces on exit.Covers the normal-completion path too. Leaked tasks are the classic async production problem.
"Single-process only" in the docstringStates the limitation honestly.Important. This registry is in memory, so it works with one uvicorn worker and breaks with several — the decision may hit a different process from the waiting agent. For real deployment you need Redis pub/sub, or a checkpointer (section 6.6's argument for LangGraph). Say so rather than shipping a subtle bug.

M15 is done. git commit -m "M15: FastAPI with SSE streaming, cancellation and approvals". The Angular app from Part 9 now has a real backend, including the round-trip that makes the approval dialog function.

Try this yourself. Ask something that triggers write_file, then do not answer the dialog. After five minutes the agent receives a denial and continues gracefully — the timeout path. Now run uvicorn --workers 2 and try again: it will hang, because the decision landed in the other process. That failure is the argument for a shared store, discovered rather than described.

10.4 Config, logging, and what to record on every call

Section 7.6 listed what to log. This is that list, implemented, with two things people forget: a trace id that ties a request together, and redaction so you do not write an API key into your own logs.

Structured JSON logs with a per-request trace id and automatic secret redaction.

"""Structured logging with a trace id, and secret redaction."""

import json
import logging
import re
import sys
import time
import uuid
from contextvars import ContextVar
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

trace_id_var: ContextVar[str] = ContextVar("trace_id", default="-")

SECRET_PATTERNS = [
    re.compile(r"(?i)\b(gsk|sk|hf|xai)_[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{8,}"),
    re.compile(r"(?i)(api[_-]?key|token|secret|password)\"?\s*[:=]\s*\"?([^\"\s,}]+)"),
    re.compile(r"\bBearer\s+[A-Za-z0-9._\-]+"),
]


def redact_secrets(text: str) -> str:
    for pattern in SECRET_PATTERNS:
        text = pattern.sub(lambda m: _mask(m.group(0)), text)
    return text


def _mask(found: str) -> str:
    keep = 4 if len(found) > 12 else 0
    return (found[:keep] + "***REDACTED***") if keep else "***REDACTED***"


class JsonFormatter(logging.Formatter):
    def format(self, record: logging.LogRecord) -> str:
        payload = {
            "ts": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S", time.gmtime(record.created)),
            "level": record.levelname,
            "logger": record.name,
            "trace_id": trace_id_var.get(),
            "msg": redact_secrets(record.getMessage()),
        }
        for key, value in getattr(record, "extra_fields", {}).items():
            payload[key] = value
        if record.exc_info:
            payload["error"] = self.formatException(record.exc_info).splitlines()[-1]
        return json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False)


def setup_logging(level: str = "INFO") -> None:
    handler = logging.StreamHandler(sys.stdout)
    handler.setFormatter(JsonFormatter())
    root = logging.getLogger()
    root.handlers = [handler]
    root.setLevel(level)


def log_event(logger: logging.Logger, message: str, **fields) -> None:
    logger.info(message, extra={"extra_fields": fields})


@dataclass
class LlmCallRecord:
    """Everything section 7.6 said to record on every model call."""
    model: str
    prompt_tokens: int
    completion_tokens: int
    seconds: float
    ttft: float | None = None
    cached: bool = False
    prompt_version: str = "unset"
    step: int | None = None
    tool: str | None = None
    tool_ok: bool | None = None
    retrieved: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    citations_verified: int | None = None
    cost_usd: float = 0.0

    def as_fields(self) -> dict:
        return {k: v for k, v in self.__dict__.items() if v is not None}


if __name__ == "__main__":
    setup_logging()
    log = logging.getLogger("secondbrain.api")

    trace_id_var.set(str(uuid.uuid4())[:8])

    log_event(log, "request.start", route="/api/chat/stream", question_chars=42)

    record = LlmCallRecord(
        model="qwen3:1.7b", prompt_tokens=812, completion_tokens=96,
        seconds=6.4, ttft=0.41, prompt_version="2026-09-01",
        step=1, tool="search_notes", tool_ok=True,
        retrieved=["setup.md#4", "hardware.md#9"], citations_verified=1,
    )
    log_event(log, "llm.call", **record.as_fields())

    log.warning('upstream said {"api_key": "gsk_Zm9vYmFyYmF6cXV1eA", "error": "bad"}')
    log.info("Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9")

    try:
        raise TimeoutError("model did not respond in 120s")
    except TimeoutError:
        log.exception("llm.failed")
Line(s)What it doesWhy we need it
ContextVar("trace_id")Request-scoped storage that works across await points.A plain global would leak between concurrent requests; thread-local storage does not follow coroutines. ContextVar is the correct tool for exactly this, and the middleware in 10.2 sets it.
JsonFormatter emitting one JSON object per lineMachine-readable logs.You can grep, pipe to jq, or ship to any log store and filter by trace_id. Human-readable log lines become useless the moment you have concurrency.
redact_secrets applied in the formatterRedaction happens at the single choke point.The important design decision. Redacting at each call site means one forgotten call leaks a key forever. Doing it in the formatter means everything that reaches a log is filtered, including third-party library messages you do not control.
the gsk|sk|hf|xai patternMatches common API key prefixes.Providers use recognisable prefixes precisely so keys can be detected. Add yours.
the Bearer patternCatches auth headers.Because at 2am you will log the full request headers "just to see", and that is how tokens end up in a log aggregator.
_mask keeping four charactersShows a prefix for long secrets.Lets you tell which key was used without revealing it. For short strings it redacts entirely, since four characters of a short secret is a meaningful fraction of it.
extra={"extra_fields": fields}Passes arbitrary structured fields through the logging API.Python's logging has no native structured-field concept, so this is the standard workaround. Keeps log_event(log, "llm.call", model=..., tokens=...) pleasant to write.
splitlines()[-1] on the tracebackLogs only the final exception line.A full traceback in a JSON field is unreadable and enormous. The last line names the exception and message; the full trace belongs in an error tracker.
LlmCallRecord with prompt_versionRecords which prompt template produced this call.Section 3.7's VERSION. Without it, next month's "quality dropped" investigation cannot tell whether the prompt or the model changed.
retrieved: list[str]The chunk ids that went into the prompt.Makes a bad answer diagnosable: you can see exactly what the model was looking at. This single field saves more debugging time than everything else here.
as_fields() dropping NoneOmits fields that do not apply.A non-streaming call has no ttft and a retrieval call has no tool. Null-filled log lines are noise.

Verified output

{"ts": "2026-09-01T08:06:31", "level": "INFO", "logger": "secondbrain.api",
 "trace_id": "7f4525ac", "msg": "request.start", "route": "/api/chat/stream",
 "question_chars": 42}

{"ts": "2026-09-01T08:06:31", "level": "INFO", "logger": "secondbrain.api",
 "trace_id": "7f4525ac", "msg": "llm.call", "model": "qwen3:1.7b",
 "prompt_tokens": 812, "completion_tokens": 96, "seconds": 6.4, "ttft": 0.41,
 "cached": false, "prompt_version": "2026-09-01", "step": 1,
 "tool": "search_notes", "tool_ok": true,
 "retrieved": ["setup.md#4", "hardware.md#9"], "citations_verified": 1,
 "cost_usd": 0.0}

{"ts": "...", "level": "WARNING", "trace_id": "7f4525ac",
 "msg": "upstream said {\"api_***REDACTED***\", \"error\": \"bad\"}"}

{"ts": "...", "level": "INFO", "trace_id": "7f4525ac",
 "msg": "Authorization: Bear***REDACTED***"}

{"ts": "...", "level": "ERROR", "trace_id": "7f4525ac", "msg": "llm.failed",
 "error": "TimeoutError: model did not respond in 120s"}

Both secrets are gone, every line shares the trace id, and the llm.call line alone answers "what did the model see, how long did it take, and did the citations verify" — which is most of what you ever need.

Regex redaction is not a compliance control. Section 6.10 made the same point about PII: patterns catch the obvious cases and will miss novel formats. Combine it with (a) never logging full request bodies in production, (b) a deliberate retention policy, and (c) redacting user content too if your prompts carry personal data — which, in a document-search product, they do.

Try this yourself. Add your own Groq key to a log line and confirm it is masked. Then add it in an unusual shape — split across a dict, or base64-encoded — and watch it get through. That is the honest limit of pattern matching, and the reason not to log request bodies at all.

10.5 M14a — tracing with Langfuse

Structured logs tell you what happened. A trace shows you the shape: this request called the agent, which called the retriever, which called the embedder, and step 3 took 4 seconds. For agents that distinction matters more than anywhere else in software, because the interesting bugs are in the sequence.

Self-hosting it

  langfuse:
    image: langfuse/langfuse:latest
    container_name: sb-langfuse
    depends_on:
      - langfuse-db
    ports:
      - "3000:3000"
    environment:
      - DATABASE_URL=postgresql://langfuse:langfuse@langfuse-db:5432/langfuse
      - NEXTAUTH_URL=http://localhost:3000
      - NEXTAUTH_SECRET=change-me-locally
      - SALT=change-me-too
      - TELEMETRY_ENABLED=false
    restart: unless-stopped

  langfuse-db:
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    container_name: sb-langfuse-db
    environment:
      - POSTGRES_USER=langfuse
      - POSTGRES_PASSWORD=langfuse
      - POSTGRES_DB=langfuse
    volumes:
      - langfuse-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    restart: unless-stopped

⚠⚠ Verify this compose block before relying on it. Langfuse's self-hosting requirements have grown — recent versions want ClickHouse, Redis and object storage alongside Postgres, and the required environment variables have changed more than once. The two-service block above reflects a simpler earlier shape and may not start a current image. Get the canonical compose file from langfuse.com/self-hosting and pin the image tag. I would rather tell you that than hand you a config that fails in a way you cannot diagnose.

Instrumenting your calls

⚠ SDK shape, not exact code. Langfuse's Python SDK has been through major versions with different import paths and decorator names (langfuse.decorators, then a top-level observe, plus an OpenTelemetry-based route). Read the current docs for the exact API. What follows is the pattern, which is stable, expressed against a thin wrapper you own — so an SDK change touches one file instead of thirty.

"""Tracing wrapper. Swap the backend here; the rest of the app never changes."""

import logging
import time
from contextlib import contextmanager

from app.config import get_settings
from app.obs import log_event, trace_id_var

log = logging.getLogger("secondbrain.trace")

_client = None


def _get_client():
    """Lazily build a Langfuse client, or None if tracing is off."""
    global _client
    settings = get_settings()
    if not settings.langfuse_enabled:
        return None
    if _client is None:
        try:
            from langfuse import Langfuse            # ⚠ verify the import path
            _client = Langfuse(
                public_key=settings.langfuse_public_key,
                secret_key=settings.langfuse_secret_key,
                host=settings.langfuse_host,
            )
        except Exception as exc:                     # noqa: BLE001
            log_event(log, "tracing.unavailable", error=str(exc))
            _client = None
    return _client


@contextmanager
def span(name: str, kind: str = "span", **attributes):
    """Time a unit of work. Always logs; also traces when Langfuse is configured."""
    started = time.perf_counter()
    client = _get_client()
    handle = None

    if client is not None:
        try:
            handle = client.start_span(name=name, input=attributes)  # ⚠ verify
        except Exception:                            # noqa: BLE001
            handle = None

    try:
        yield handle
    except Exception as exc:
        log_event(log, f"{name}.error", kind=kind, error=str(exc),
                  ms=round((time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000))
        if handle is not None:
            try:
                handle.end(level="ERROR", status_message=str(exc))
            except Exception:                        # noqa: BLE001
                pass
        raise
    else:
        log_event(log, f"{name}.ok", kind=kind, trace_id=trace_id_var.get(),
                  ms=round((time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000), **attributes)
        if handle is not None:
            try:
                handle.end()
            except Exception:                        # noqa: BLE001
                pass


def flush() -> None:
    """Call on shutdown. The SDK batches, so unflushed spans are lost."""
    client = _get_client()
    if client is not None:
        try:
            client.flush()
        except Exception:                            # noqa: BLE001
            pass
Line(s)What it doesWhy we need it
a wrapper module at allAll tracing goes through span().The main lesson of this section. Given how fast this SDK moves, sprinkling @observe() through thirty files makes the next upgrade a migration. One wrapper makes it a one-file edit — and lets you swap Langfuse for Phoenix or raw OpenTelemetry without touching the app.
if not settings.langfuse_enabled: return NoneTracing is optional.The course must run with no accounts and no extra containers. Tracing off means logging still happens.
try/except around client constructionA missing package or unreachable host disables tracing rather than crashing.Observability must never take down the thing it observes. This is a rule, not a nicety — a tracing outage becoming an application outage is a real and embarrassing incident.
@contextmanagerGives you with span("retrieve", top_k=4):.Timing and error handling in one construct that cannot be forgotten on an early return.
always calling log_eventLogs regardless of whether tracing is on.Section 7.6's point that plain structured logging gets you 70% of the value. The trace is an upgrade, not a replacement.
except Exception ... raiseRecords the failure, then re-raises.The span must be closed with an error status, but the exception belongs to the caller. Swallowing it here would hide real bugs.
nested try/except around every SDK callEven end() is defensive.Ugly, and deliberate. Any of these can fail if the SDK version differs from what you expect, and none of them should break a user's request.
flush()Forces batched spans out.Easy to forget. The SDK batches for efficiency, so a process that exits without flushing loses its most recent traces — exactly the ones you were looking at. Call it in the lifespan teardown.

Where to put spans

from app.tracing import span

# One span per request, one per meaningful unit of work inside it.
with span("chat.request", question_chars=len(question)):
    with span("retrieve", kind="retriever", top_k=4) as s:
        chunks = retrieve(question, top_k=4)

    with span("rerank", kind="reranker", candidates=len(chunks)):
        chunks = rerank(question, chunks, top_k=4)

    with span("generate", kind="generation", model=settings.chat_model) as s:
        answer = generate(question, chunks)

    with span("verify_citations", claimed=len(answer.citations)):
        good, problems = verify_citations(...)
SpanWhat its duration tells you
chat.requestTotal user-perceived latency. The number to put on a dashboard.
retrieveEmbedding plus search. Usually tens of milliseconds; if it is seconds, the embedder is being reloaded per request (10.2's lifespan fix).
rerankThe cross-encoder. Grows linearly with candidate count — this is where candidates=50 shows up as 300 ms.
generateNearly all of your latency, on a local model.
verify_citationsMicroseconds, but the attributes matter: claimed versus verified counts, tracked over time, is a hallucination early-warning signal.
Deeper dive: OpenTelemetry, and why it is the safer bet long term

Section 7.6 mentioned the OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions. The argument for them over a vendor SDK: your spans become portable, they join the same pipeline as your other services, and the attribute names are standardised (model name, token counts, and so on) rather than vendor-specific. Langfuse, Phoenix and others can ingest OTel data.

The argument against, today: ⚠ the GenAI conventions are still evolving and attribute names have changed, and the vendor SDKs give you a better out-of-the-box UI for LLM-shaped data. The pragmatic position is exactly the wrapper above — one file that decides how spans are emitted, so switching to OTel later is a contained change rather than a rewrite.

10.6 M14b — evals in CI, with a gate

Section 5.13 built the eval harness. This turns it into something that blocks a merge, which is the difference between having evals and being protected by them.

Compare this run against a stored baseline and fail on either an absolute floor or a regression.

"""Regression gate: run the eval suite and fail CI if quality dropped."""

import json
import sys
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass
from pathlib import Path

BASELINE = Path("backend/evals/baseline.json")

THRESHOLDS = {
    "recall_at_5":          {"min": 0.70, "max_drop": 0.05},
    "mrr":                  {"min": 0.60, "max_drop": 0.05},
    "citation_verified":    {"min": 0.90, "max_drop": 0.03},
    "abstention_correct":   {"min": 0.80, "max_drop": 0.05},
    "format_valid":         {"min": 0.95, "max_drop": 0.02},
}


@dataclass
class Metrics:
    recall_at_5: float
    mrr: float
    citation_verified: float
    abstention_correct: float
    format_valid: float
    mean_latency_s: float
    mean_tokens: int


def compare(current: Metrics, baseline: Metrics | None) -> tuple[bool, list[str]]:
    """Return (passed, messages). Fails on an absolute floor or a regression."""
    messages, ok = [], True
    now = asdict(current)
    was = asdict(baseline) if baseline else {}

    for name, rule in THRESHOLDS.items():
        value = now[name]
        if value < rule["min"]:
            ok = False
            messages.append(f"FAIL {name}={value:.3f} below floor {rule['min']:.2f}")
            continue
        if name in was:
            drop = was[name] - value
            if drop > rule["max_drop"]:
                ok = False
                messages.append(
                    f"FAIL {name} regressed {drop:.3f} "
                    f"({was[name]:.3f} -> {value:.3f}), limit {rule['max_drop']:.2f}"
                )
            else:
                arrow = "+" if value >= was[name] else "-"
                messages.append(f"ok   {name}={value:.3f} ({arrow}{abs(value-was[name]):.3f})")
        else:
            messages.append(f"ok   {name}={value:.3f} (no baseline)")

    if baseline and current.mean_latency_s > baseline.mean_latency_s * 1.5:
        messages.append(
            f"WARN latency {baseline.mean_latency_s:.1f}s -> {current.mean_latency_s:.1f}s"
        )
    return ok, messages


def load_baseline(path: Path = BASELINE) -> Metrics | None:
    if not path.exists():
        return None
    return Metrics(**json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")))


def save_baseline(metrics: Metrics, path: Path = BASELINE) -> None:
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_text(json.dumps(asdict(metrics), indent=2), encoding="utf-8")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    baseline = Metrics(recall_at_5=0.82, mrr=0.71, citation_verified=0.96,
                       abstention_correct=0.88, format_valid=1.0,
                       mean_latency_s=6.2, mean_tokens=910)
    save_baseline(baseline)

    print("=== run 1: a small genuine improvement ===")
    better = Metrics(0.85, 0.74, 0.97, 0.88, 1.0, 6.0, 905)
    ok, msgs = compare(better, load_baseline())
    for m in msgs: print("  " + m)
    print(f"  gate: {'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'}")

    print("\n=== run 2: chunk size changed, retrieval regressed ===")
    worse = Metrics(0.63, 0.55, 0.94, 0.86, 0.99, 9.8, 1450)
    ok, msgs = compare(worse, load_baseline())
    for m in msgs: print("  " + m)
    print(f"  gate: {'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'}")

    print("\n=== run 3: fine-tune broke abstention (the Part 8 risk) ===")
    tuned = Metrics(0.83, 0.72, 0.95, 0.55, 1.0, 3.1, 400)
    ok, msgs = compare(tuned, load_baseline())
    for m in msgs: print("  " + m)
    print(f"  gate: {'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'}")
    sys.exit(0)
Line(s)What it doesWhy we need it
THRESHOLDS with both min and max_dropTwo independent checks per metric.A floor catches "this is not good enough to ship". A drop limit catches "this got worse than yesterday" even when both numbers are above the floor. You need both: without the floor, quality can erode 4% per week forever; without the drop limit, a single bad change hides under a generous floor.
citation_verified in the metric setFraction of claimed citations that verified against the retrieved text.Section 5.7's check, turned into a tracked metric. Its floor of 0.90 with a tight 0.03 drop limit reflects that a fall here means fabrication — the most serious regression in a RAG system.
abstention_correctHow often the system correctly says "not in the documents".The metric that catches the Part 8 fine-tuning risk. Nothing else in the suite would notice that you trained away the ability to say "I don't know".
format_validFraction of responses that parsed against the Pydantic schema.Catches a model or prompt change breaking structured output. Its floor is 0.95 because below that your retry loop (section 3.4) is quietly paying a tax.
latency as a warning, not a failureReports a 50% slowdown without blocking.CI machines vary too much for a hard latency gate — you would get flaky failures and people would disable the whole thing. Warn, and watch the trend.
if baseline is None pathPasses with "no baseline".The first run has nothing to compare against. It must not fail, or nobody can ever adopt this.
save_baseline as a separate functionUpdating the baseline is deliberate.Policy point: the baseline should be regenerated on the main branch after a reviewed improvement, never automatically from a feature branch. Auto-updating turns the gate into a rubber stamp that ratchets downwards.
messages including the deltaPrints (+0.030) or (-0.020).A reviewer reads CI output for four seconds. Show them the direction and size, not just pass or fail.

Verified output — three realistic runs

=== run 1: a small genuine improvement ===
  ok   recall_at_5=0.850 (+0.030)
  ok   mrr=0.740 (+0.030)
  ok   citation_verified=0.970 (+0.010)
  ok   abstention_correct=0.880 (+0.000)
  ok   format_valid=1.000 (+0.000)
  gate: PASS

=== run 2: chunk size changed, retrieval regressed ===
  FAIL recall_at_5=0.630 below floor 0.70
  FAIL mrr=0.550 below floor 0.60
  ok   citation_verified=0.940 (-0.020)
  ok   abstention_correct=0.860 (-0.020)
  ok   format_valid=0.990 (-0.010)
  WARN latency 6.2s -> 9.8s
  gate: FAIL

=== run 3: fine-tune broke abstention (the Part 8 risk) ===
  ok   recall_at_5=0.830 (+0.010)
  ok   mrr=0.720 (+0.010)
  ok   citation_verified=0.950 (-0.010)
  FAIL abstention_correct=0.550 below floor 0.80
  ok   format_valid=1.000 (+0.000)
  gate: FAIL

Run 3 is the one to study. Retrieval improved slightly, citations held, format was perfect, latency halved to 3.1 seconds and token use dropped from 910 to 400 — by every metric a developer would look at, the fine-tuned model is better and cheaper. And it is unshippable, because it lost the ability to say "I don't know", which the gate caught. That is precisely the failure section 8.1 warned about, detected automatically rather than discovered by a user.

The CI workflow

name: ci

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  backend:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v5
      - run: uv venv --python 3.13
      - run: uv pip install -r backend/requirements-dev.txt
      - name: Lint and type check
        run: |
          uv run ruff check backend
          uv run mypy backend/app
      - name: Unit tests with a fake model
        env:
          LLM_BACKEND: echo
        run: uv run pytest backend/tests -q
      - name: Retrieval evals (no LLM needed)
        run: uv run python backend/evals/eval_retrieval.py
      - name: Regression gate
        run: uv run python backend/evals/regress.py

  frontend:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: frontend/package-lock.json
      - run: npm ci
        working-directory: frontend
      - run: npm run test -- --run
        working-directory: frontend
      - run: npm run build
        working-directory: frontend
Line(s)What it doesWhy we need it
LLM_BACKEND: echoRuns the unit tests against section 4.1's EchoBackend.The reason CI is fast and deterministic. No model download, no GPU, no rate limits, no flakiness. That backend was written in Part 4 for exactly this moment.
retrieval evals as their own stepRuns recall@k and MRR with no LLM.Section 5.13's point: these need no judge model, so they can run on every pull request in seconds. Judged metrics are slower and noisier — run those nightly.
the regression gate as the last stepFails the job on a quality drop.Ordering is deliberate: lint, then types, then unit tests, then quality. Fail on the cheapest signal first so contributors get feedback in seconds.
npm run test -- --runRuns the frontend tests once and exits.Vitest watches by default (section 9.14), which hangs a CI job forever. ⚠ Check the flag your runner expects.
npm ci, not npm installInstalls exactly the lockfile.Reproducible, and fails if the lockfile is out of date rather than silently updating it.
npm run build in CIBuilds the production bundle.Catches template type errors and bundle-budget failures (section 9.13) that ng serve tolerates.

M14 is done. git commit -m "M14: tracing, structured logs and a CI regression gate".

Try this yourself. Change CHUNK_SIZE in build_index.py from 800 to 200, re-index, and run the eval suite. Watch recall@5 fall and the gate fail. You have now experienced the thing section 5.4 asserted — chunk size changes answer quality — as a red build rather than a claim.
